✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #4 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:07:54 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Responsibility (Noun)
ज़िम्मेदारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Responsibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring." (Hinglish Arth: पर्याप्त संसाधनों और निगरानी के साथ जलवायु कार्रवाई समय पर होनी चाहिए)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are..." (Hinglish Arth: जलवायु कार्रवाई समय पर होनी चाहिए, जिसके लिए केंद्र सरकार को पर्याप्त संसाधन समर्पित करने चाहिए और सक्रिय रूप से यह सुनिश्चित करना चाहिए कि उसकी पहल लागू हो।)

From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number. These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Election Commission of India / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / election / India

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #5 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:31:27 PM IST
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number. These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Election Commission of India / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / election / India

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again. That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Ukraine / USA / Russia-Ukraine Crisis / war / war

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — रूस, यूक्रेन और अमेरिका के बीच अबू धाबी में त्रिपक्षीय वार्ता। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Trilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: त्रिपक्षीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Trilateral' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — इस महीने की शुरुआत में कोई बड़ी सफलता हासिल करने या कीव और मॉस्को के बीच व्यापक अंतर को पाटने में विफल रही।।

hinglishTracks.en: Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — फिर भी, वे द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के बाद यूरोप के सबसे लंबे युद्ध का राजनीतिक समाधान खोजने की दिशा में एक अच्छी शुरुआत थे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Settlement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: बस्ती — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Settlement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — अमेरिका द्वारा आयोजित दो दिवसीय वार्ता में, युद्धरत पक्ष कैदियों की अदला-बदली सहित कुछ मानवीय उपायों पर सहमत हुए।।

hinglishTracks.en: representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — प्रस्ताव पर चर्चा के लिए प्रतिनिधि जेरेड कुशनर और स्टीव विटकॉफ़ ने वार्ता के बाद मॉस्को में रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन से मुलाकात की।।

hinglishTracks.en: In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अगले चरण में, अमेरिकी, यूक्रेनी और यूरोपीय अधिकारी शांति प्रक्रिया के प्रति समन्वित यूरोपीय और यूक्रेनी स्थिति पर चर्चा करने के लिए बर्लिन में मिलेंगे।।

hinglishTracks.en: As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अभी तक, रूसी और यूक्रेनी स्थिति बहुत दूर हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — रूस ने हमलों को रोकने के लिए यूक्रेन से डोनबास के उन क्षेत्रों से हटने की मांग की है जिन पर उसका अभी भी नियंत्रण है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Territorial' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रादेशिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Territorial' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions).
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — रूस भी यूक्रेनी सैन्य क्षमताओं पर सीमाएं लगाना चाहता है और कीव तटस्थता की घोषणा करना चाहता है (अपनी नाटो महत्वाकांक्षाओं को छोड़ना)।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Neutrality' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: तटस्थता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Neutrality' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — दूसरी ओर, यूक्रेन ने समझौते के लिए कोई भी क्षेत्रीय रियायत देने से इनकार कर दिया है और पश्चिम से सुरक्षा गारंटी मांगी है ताकि रूस देश पर दोबारा हमला न करे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Territorial' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रादेशिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Territorial' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यूक्रेन रूस के आक्रमण से बच गया और लगभग पाँच वर्षों तक रूसी सेनाओं का विरोध करता रहा, यह कोई छोटी उपलब्धि नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — लेकिन इसने अपने प्रतिरोध की भारी कीमत भी चुकाई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The country has lost more than 20% of its territory.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — देश ने अपना 20% से अधिक क्षेत्र खो दिया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Territorial' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रादेशिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Territorial' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — लाखों लोग भाग गए हैं, जबकि लड़ने की उम्र के लोगों को सेना में शामिल किया जा रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — यूक्रेन की अर्थव्यवस्था यूरोपीय समर्थन से चलती रहती है, जबकि इसकी सेना हथियारों और अन्य आपूर्ति के लिए नाटो पर निर्भर रहती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — हाल तक, पश्चिम रूस के ख़िलाफ़ यूक्रेन के समर्थन में एकजुट था, लेकिन तब से वह एकता ख़त्म होने लगी है।।

hinglishTracks.en: President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प, जिन्होंने रूसी डीजल पर प्रतिबंध हटा दिया है, मास्को के साथ वाशिंगटन के संबंधों को फिर से स्थापित करने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — यूरोपीय नेता, जिन्होंने शुरू में रूस को अलग-थलग करने की कोशिश की थी, उन्होंने भी क्रेमलिन के साथ फिर से संपर्क स्थापित करना शुरू कर दिया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — अक्टूबर में, फिनिश और नॉर्वेजियन नेताओं ने श्री के साथ सीधी बातचीत की।।

hinglishTracks.en: To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — निश्चित रूप से, यूक्रेन के लंबी दूरी के हमले रूस को नुकसान पहुंचा सकते हैं, जैसा कि केर्च ब्रिज पर हाल के हमले से पता चला है।।

hinglishTracks.en: But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — लेकिन इस तरह के हमलों से क्रेमलिन की युद्ध के बारे में सोच बदलने की संभावना नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — जैसे-जैसे संघर्ष बढ़ता जा रहा है, यूक्रेन की स्थिति कमज़ोर होती जा रही है और उसके सहयोगियों में फूट बढ़ती जा रही है।।

hinglishTracks.en: After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — करीब पांच साल बाद रूस निर्णायक जीत हासिल करने में नाकाम रहा है.।

hinglishTracks.en: Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — यूक्रेन के पास जीत की दिशा में कोई विश्वसनीय रास्ता भी नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इसलिए, कूटनीतिक समझौता ही आगे बढ़ने का एकमात्र रास्ता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Settlement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: बस्ती — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Settlement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अबू धाबी वार्ता ने इस वास्तविकता को पहचाना।।

hinglishTracks.en: But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — लेकिन इस प्रक्रिया को सार्थक बनाने के लिए यूरोप को भी बातचीत की मेज पर लाना होगा।।

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #6 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:31:27 PM IST
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again. That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Ukraine / USA / Russia-Ukraine Crisis / war / war

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again. That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Ukraine / USA / Russia-Ukraine Crisis / war / war

articles.title: Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident. Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction. “Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added. Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist. The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly. “Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:08:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident. Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction. “Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added. Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist. The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly. “Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

Department (Adjective)
विभाग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Department' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Junction (Noun)
जंक्शन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Junction' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Location (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Location' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Chaotic (Adjective)
अराजक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Chaotic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction. “Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added. Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist. The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly. “Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said. Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said an FIR was lodged against the minors under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the BNS. All of them were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and notices were sent to their parents. According to the police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of minors surrounded them and began to abuse them. When the couple tried to reason with the group, they assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden. Police detained them after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. The police said they are recording the statements of the couple and the juveniles to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident that took place at the Pramod Mahajan Garden. The incident drew sharp reactions from political parties, with many condemning it. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra president Abu Asim Azmi said the juvenile age threshold should be brought down from 18 to 15 and that those below 18 years who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not be given concessions under the law. Mr. Azmi added that the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination. Meanwhile, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya met the couple at the Ghatkopar police station and promised action. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the Home portfolio, to “adopt a no-tolerance policy towards such incidents” and said citizens should be able to move around freely in the State. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the assault.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mumbai / law / crime / police / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / Shiv Sena

articles.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department. Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged. Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added. Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests. Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October. On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:01:11 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department. Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged. Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added. Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests. Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October. On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Availability (Noun)
उपलब्धता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Availability' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inspection (Adjective / Verb)
निरीक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Inspection' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

A. Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, s' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former..." (Hinglish Arth: यह आरोप लगाते हुए कि रोहतक में पोस्ट-ग्रेजुएट इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ मेडिकल साइंसेज (पीजीआईएमएस) में स्वीकृत ग्रुप ए पदों में से 41.6% पद खाली पड़े हैं, हरियाणा के पूर्व गृह मंत्री सुभाष बत्रा ने रविवार को भाजपा सरकार पर सवाल उठाया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister"?

B. “The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not..." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: To mark World Diabetes Day 2026, the Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMC), Vellore, organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers in Vellore.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: According to a press release, participants have to write an essay on “From classroom to community – Children leading the fight against diabetes”. Around 185 students participated in various competitions at the event. Winners of the painting competition are Shavitha, Government Higher Secondary School in Poigai (Vellore), Siddharth of Shristi School (Vellore) and Ashwanth, IDA Scudder school, won first, second and third prizes respectively.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 CMC honours essay, painting, quiz competition winners in Vellore

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:00:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: To mark World Diabetes Day 2026, the Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMC), Vellore, organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers in Vellore.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: According to a press release, participants have to write an essay on “From classroom to community – Children leading the fight against diabetes”. Painting competition was “From screen time to Green time – keep diabetes away”. Quiz competition for teachers was related to general knowledge and non-communicable diseases. Around 185 students participated in various competitions at the event. Winners of the painting competition are Shavitha, Government Higher Secondary School in Poigai (Vellore), Siddharth of Shristi School (Vellore) and Ashwanth, IDA Scudder school, won first, second and third prizes respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In the teachers quiz competition, Savitha and Sreeja of Sunbeam CBSE School. Muthanara. and Anushya - Spark School, Savitha and Monisha of Shrishti Vidyashram School won first, second and third prizes respectively, the release said.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector. The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids. Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said. The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines. “Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement. Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: coal / economy (general) / business (general) / minerals (general) / metal and mineral / mining / natural resources (general) / energy resources / energy and resource

📰 Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:31:26 PM IST

1. Core Context & Background: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector. The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids. Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said. The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines. “Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement. Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years. Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues. They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary. As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year. “The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow. Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”. Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances. “The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:47:07 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years. Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues. They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary. As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year. “The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow. Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”. Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances. “The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility

Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive..." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive"?

B. Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party.

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party." (Hinglish Arth: उत्तर प्रदेश/कार्यकारी (सरकार)/भारतीय जनता पार्टी)

Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues. They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary. As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year. “The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow. Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”. Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances. “The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides. Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22). "The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement. "A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details. A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 10:46:53 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides. Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22). "The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement. "A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details. A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".
