hinglishTracks.en: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — नेपाल के पीएम ने कहा, "भारत और नेपाल के बीच संबंध हिमालय जितने मजबूत और महासागर जितने विशाल हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्रधान मंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने सोमवार (23 नवंबर, 2026) को अपने नेपाली समकक्ष बालेंद्र शाह के साथ व्यापक बातचीत के बाद नेपाल के लिए 24,000 करोड़ नेपाली रुपये के विकास पैकेज की घोषणा की, जिससे द्विपक्षीय संबंधों को और मजबूत करने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण परिणाम सामने आए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Bilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत। इसके Synonyms हैं: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual और Antonyms हैं: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way।

hinglishTracks.en: The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — दोनों नेताओं ने वस्तुतः नेपाल में कई भारत समर्थित परियोजनाओं की नींव रखी और उत्तर प्रदेश में अयोध्या और नेपाल में जनकपुर धाम के बीच सीमा पार यात्री रेल लिंक को हरी झंडी दिखाई।।

hinglishTracks.en: Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — नेपाल के पीएम शाह रविवार (22 नवंबर) को दो दिवसीय यात्रा पर नई दिल्ली पहुंचे, जिसका इरादा द्विपक्षीय संबंधों में नई गति लाने का था, जो भारत और नेपाल के बीच लंबे समय से चले आ रहे सीमा विवाद को सुलझाने के लिए चीन और यूनाइटेड किंगडम को शामिल करने की पीएम शाह की टिप्पणी के बाद मई में कुछ तनाव में आ गए थे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Bilateral' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत। इसके Synonyms हैं: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual और Antonyms हैं: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way।

hinglishTracks.en: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — नेपाली नेता ने अपने मीडिया बयान में कहा, "भारत और नेपाल के बीच संबंध हिमालय जितने मजबूत और महासागर जितने विशाल हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उन्होंने कहा, ''एक भरोसेमंद और विश्वसनीय पड़ोसी के रूप में, भारत नेपाल में प्राकृतिक आपदाओं और कठिन समय में लगातार प्रथम प्रतिक्रियाकर्ता के रूप में खड़ा रहा।'' उन्होंने कहा कि आपसी सम्मान, दृढ़ विश्वास और अटूट सद्भावना संबंधों का आधार हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: In his remarks, Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अपनी टिप्पणी में, मोदी ने भारत-नेपाल संबंधों की ताकत पर भी प्रकाश डाला और बताया कि कैसे नई दिल्ली पड़ोसी देश के विकास और समृद्धि के लिए हर संभव सहायता देने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — “भारत और नेपाल के बीच का रिश्ता सिर्फ पड़ोसियों का नहीं है, बल्कि यह रिश्तेदारी और अटूट विश्वास का है।।

hinglishTracks.en: We share our joys and challenges," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — हम अपनी खुशियाँ और चुनौतियाँ साझा करते हैं," उन्होंने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उन्होंने कहा, "हम एक-दूसरे की प्रगति में भागीदार हैं और कठिन समय में एक-दूसरे के समर्थन का स्रोत हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: The prime minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — प्रधानमंत्री ने अगस्त में नेपाल में आई विनाशकारी बाढ़ से हुई जानमाल की हानि पर भारत की ओर से गहरी संवेदना व्यक्त की।।

hinglishTracks.en: "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने कहा, "और आज, नेपाल के पुनर्निर्माण और दीर्घकालिक विकास को नई ताकत देने के लिए, हमने 24,000 करोड़ नेपाली रुपये के विकास सहयोग पैकेज की घोषणा की।"। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Reconstruction' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Reconstruction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — पीएम मोदी ने ऊर्जा क्षेत्र में नेपाल को भारत की मदद का भी जिक्र किया.।

hinglishTracks.en: "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — "भारत कई वर्षों से नेपाल को पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं का एक विश्वसनीय आपूर्तिकर्ता रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — हमारी पड़ोसी प्रथम नीति की भावना को ध्यान में रखते हुए, इस वर्ष तेल आपूर्ति से संबंधित गंभीर चुनौतियों के बावजूद, हमने नेपाल को ईंधन, उर्वरक और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं की आपूर्ति बनाए रखी है, ”उन्होंने कहा।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 India announces development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese Rupees for Nepal’s development

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:24:21 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties. The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal. "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement. "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations. In his remarks, Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation. "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust. We share our joys and challenges," he said. "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said. The prime minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector. "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, we have maintained the supply of fuel, fertilisers and other essential goods to Nepal," he said.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties. The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal. "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement. "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations. In his remarks, Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation. "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust. We share our joys and challenges," he said. "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said. The prime minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector. "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, we have maintained the supply of fuel, fertilisers and other essential goods to Nepal," he said.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from Kallakurichi Collector over TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to take instructions from the woman officer, too, and report to the court by November 24, 2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arun Vignesh of misbehaving with her, as widely reported in the media over the past few days. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer. When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case. “Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?” The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.” On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.” Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: After taking note of the SPP’s submission that the State was willing to file an affidavit before the court making it clear that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received any complaint from the woman IAS officer, the judge asked Mr. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any complaint.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from Kallakurichi Collector over TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:23:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to take instructions from the woman officer, too, and report to the court by November 24, 2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arun Vignesh of misbehaving with her, as widely reported in the media over the past few days. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer. When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case. “Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?” The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.” On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.” Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: After taking note of the SPP’s submission that the State was willing to file an affidavit before the court making it clear that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received any complaint from the woman IAS officer, the judge asked Mr. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any complaint.

Representation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Representation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Harassment (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Harassment' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Commission (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Commission' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Cognisance (Noun)
संज्ञान — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Cognisance' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from Kallakurichi Collector over TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive compl' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive co' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive co' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R." (Hinglish Arth: लक्ष्मीनारायणन ने राज्य लोक अभियोजक आर. से पूछा।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from Kallakurichi Collector over TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any..." (Hinglish Arth: सथ्यन को महिला आईएएस अधिकारी से भी संपर्क करने और मंगलवार (24 नवंबर, 2026) तक निर्देश प्राप्त करने को कहा है कि क्या उन्होंने कोई शिकायत दर्ज कराई है।)

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur. Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees. Regular weekly services will begin on November 28. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’. Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said. Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship. It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations. Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur. Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees. Regular weekly services will begin on November 28. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’. Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said. Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship. It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations. Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.

articles.title: India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, economist Prabhat Patanaik spoke at a seminar titled ‘The new age of imperialism’ organised by Sitaram Yechury foundation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India is facing challenges on several fronts which includes a gradual movement towards an authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Hamid Ansari said. Mr. Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan, highlighted three point challenges faced by the country, which includes the pursuit of neoliberal policies, sharpening of communal polarisation and the movement towards authoritarian rule. “This threefold attack includes the aggressive pursuit of neoliberal policies of economic reforms. Secondly, the relentless onslaught on the secular democratic foundations of the Indian republic by sharpening of communal polarisation, and thirdly, the movement towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions and methods of which are considered sacrosanct in a democracy,” the former Vice-President said. Recalling the contribution of the late Sitaram Yechury. Mr Ansari said that the CPI(M) spoke against the certain ideological position in which nationalism has only been equated with Hindu nationalism. “Bharat Mata has no Hinduism in naturalism. This is not a Bharat Mata that has given birth to Muslims, Christians, Tarsus, Buddhists, Jains, and atheists,” Mr. Ansari quoted Mr. Yechury from one of his speeches in 2017. The former Vice-President also said Mr. Yechury opined that the struggle against imperialist aggression, the imposition of neoliberal order, and fundamentalism should be welded together to form a powerful anti-imperialist movement. He emphasised the need to maintain multilateralism in external affairs so as not to compromise on foreign policy positions, Mr. Ansari recalled that Mr. Yechury, despite some frictions within the CPI(M) and with the Congress, formed a strong relationship with the Congress leadership, particularly with Sonia Gandhi and the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi. He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government. He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. This is usually strange. The Congress accepted many of the suggestions to ensure a working majority,” he added. Meanwhile, general secretary of CPI(M) M.A. Baby, Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera, renowned economist Prabhat Patnaik, historian Mukul Kesavan, and distinguished scholar Malini Bhattacharya were also present in the seminar in Kolkata on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing the seminar, Mr. Baby said that imperialism has reached a diabolical and barbaric stage across the world today. “Before Israel was to launch an attack on Iran without any rhyme or reason, the Prime Minister of India goes to Israel and addresses the Israeli Parliament two days ahead oftime. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:21:06 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, economist Prabhat Patanaik spoke at a seminar titled ‘The new age of imperialism’ organised by Sitaram Yechury foundation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India is facing challenges on several fronts which includes a gradual movement towards an authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Hamid Ansari said. Mr. Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan, highlighted three point challenges faced by the country, which includes the pursuit of neoliberal policies, sharpening of communal polarisation and the movement towards authoritarian rule. “This threefold attack includes the aggressive pursuit of neoliberal policies of economic reforms. Secondly, the relentless onslaught on the secular democratic foundations of the Indian republic by sharpening of communal polarisation, and thirdly, the movement towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions and methods of which are considered sacrosanct in a democracy,” the former Vice-President said. Recalling the contribution of the late Sitaram Yechury. Mr Ansari said that the CPI(M) spoke against the certain ideological position in which nationalism has only been equated with Hindu nationalism. “Bharat Mata has no Hinduism in naturalism. This is not a Bharat Mata that has given birth to Muslims, Christians, Tarsus, Buddhists, Jains, and atheists,” Mr. Ansari quoted Mr. Yechury from one of his speeches in 2017. The former Vice-President also said Mr. Yechury opined that the struggle against imperialist aggression, the imposition of neoliberal order, and fundamentalism should be welded together to form a powerful anti-imperialist movement. He emphasised the need to maintain multilateralism in external affairs so as not to compromise on foreign policy positions, Mr. Ansari recalled that Mr. Yechury, despite some frictions within the CPI(M) and with the Congress, formed a strong relationship with the Congress leadership, particularly with Sonia Gandhi and the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi. He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government. He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. This is usually strange. The Congress accepted many of the suggestions to ensure a working majority,” he added. Meanwhile, general secretary of CPI(M) M.A. Baby, Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera, renowned economist Prabhat Patnaik, historian Mukul Kesavan, and distinguished scholar Malini Bhattacharya were also present in the seminar in Kolkata on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing the seminar, Mr. Baby said that imperialism has reached a diabolical and barbaric stage across the world today. “Before Israel was to launch an attack on Iran without any rhyme or reason, the Prime Minister of India goes to Israel and addresses the Israeli Parliament two days ahead oftime. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Multilateral (Adjective)
बहुपक्षीय — जिसमें दो से अधिक देश (जैसे UN, G20, BRICS) मिलकर साझा फैसला लेते हैं।
✓ Syn: Plurilateral, International, Coalition-based  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, One-sided, Isolated
Polarisation (Noun)
ध्रुवीकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Polarisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Contribution (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Contribution' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'India moving towards authoritarian rule through ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'India moving towards authoritarian rule throu' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'India moving towards authoritarian rule throu' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A." (Hinglish Arth: पूर्व उपराष्ट्रपति हामिद अंसारी के साथ सीपीआई (एम) महासचिव एम.ए.)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism." (Hinglish Arth: हम यहीं रह रहे हैं,” उन्होंने साम्राज्यवाद के आक्रामक विस्तार के खिलाफ वाम दलों के संघर्ष को याद करते हुए कहा।)

articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission on a PIL seeking comprehensive reforms in the anti-defection framework. The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments. Besides the Election Commission and the law panel, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notices to the Ministries of Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the PIL filed by A. Sethu. The PIL, filed through lawyers R. Satish Kumar and Jatin, sought directions to prevent misuse of “strategic resignations” by MPs and lawmakers from legislative assemblies to evade discipline of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution. It also sought directions to “(ii) secure time-bound, reasoned and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings; (iii) secure institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism; and (iv) reaffirm that in a hung Legislative Assembly, majority to form the Government must be tested only on the floor of a duly constituted House after Members are sworn under Article 188, and not through extra-parliamentary letters of support or demonstrations.” The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit. The plea said such resignations can be used to facilitate political realignments, alter the numerical strength of legislative assemblies and potentially enable elected representatives to evade the consequences contemplated under the anti-defection law. “Declare and direct that a resignation tendered by a Member of Parliament or a Member of a State Legislative Assembly, at a stage when disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution are pending or reasonably imminent against such member, shall not ipso facto terminate or render infructuous such disqualification proceedings, and that the Speaker/Chairman shall record a reasoned order, based on objective material, on both the voluntariness and genuineness of the resignation and on the disqualification petition,” the plea said. The plea sought direction to Speakers and Chairpersons to examine the voluntariness and genuineness of resignations on the basis of objective material and pass reasoned orders, while ensuring that pending disqualification proceedings are independently adjudicated.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: law / court / Election Commission of India / law enforcement

hinglishTracks.en: The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — याचिका में कहा गया है कि अयोग्यता की कार्यवाही का सामना करने वाले या प्रत्याशित विधायक अक्सर अध्यक्ष या सभापति द्वारा योग्यता के आधार पर मामलों का फैसला करने से पहले रणनीतिक इस्तीफे का सहारा लेते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Disqualification' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Disqualification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — याचिका में कहा गया है कि इस तरह के इस्तीफों का इस्तेमाल राजनीतिक पुनर्गठन को सुविधाजनक बनाने, विधान सभाओं की संख्यात्मक ताकत को बदलने और संभावित रूप से निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधियों को दलबदल विरोधी कानून के तहत अपेक्षित परिणामों से बचने में सक्षम बनाने के लिए किया जा सकता है।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 03:20:49 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission on a PIL seeking comprehensive reforms in the anti-defection framework. The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments. Besides the Election Commission and the law panel, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notices to the Ministries of Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the PIL filed by A. Sethu. The PIL, filed through lawyers R. Satish Kumar and Jatin, sought directions to prevent misuse of “strategic resignations” by MPs and lawmakers from legislative assemblies to evade discipline of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution. It also sought directions to “(ii) secure time-bound, reasoned and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings; (iii) secure institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism; and (iv) reaffirm that in a hung Legislative Assembly, majority to form the Government must be tested only on the floor of a duly constituted House after Members are sworn under Article 188, and not through extra-parliamentary letters of support or demonstrations.” The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit. The plea said such resignations can be used to facilitate political realignments, alter the numerical strength of legislative assemblies and potentially enable elected representatives to evade the consequences contemplated under the anti-defection law. “Declare and direct that a resignation tendered by a Member of Parliament or a Member of a State Legislative Assembly, at a stage when disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution are pending or reasonably imminent against such member, shall not ipso facto terminate or render infructuous such disqualification proceedings, and that the Speaker/Chairman shall record a reasoned order, based on objective material, on both the voluntariness and genuineness of the resignation and on the disqualification petition,” the plea said. The plea sought direction to Speakers and Chairpersons to examine the voluntariness and genuineness of resignations on the basis of objective material and pass reasoned orders, while ensuring that pending disqualification proceedings are independently adjudicated.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: law / court / Election Commission of India / law enforcement

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Disqualification (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Disqualification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on P' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI o' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI o' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission on a PIL seeking comprehensive reforms in the anti-defection framework. The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments. Besides the Election Commission and the law panel, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notices to the Ministries of Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the PIL filed by A. Sethu. The PIL, filed through lawyers R. Satish Kumar and Jatin, sought directions to prevent misuse of “strategic resignations” by MPs and lawmakers from legislative assemblies to evade discipline of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution. It also sought directions to “(ii) secure time-bound, reasoned and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings; (iii) secure institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism; and (iv) reaffirm that in a hung Legislative Assembly, majority to form the Government must be tested only on the floor of a duly constituted House after Members are sworn under Article 188, and not through extra-parliamentary letters of support or demonstrations.” The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit. The plea said such resignations can be used to facilitate political realignments, alter the numerical strength of legislative assemblies and potentially enable elected representatives to evade the consequences contemplated under the anti-defection law. “Declare and direct that a resignation tendered by a Member of Parliament or a Member of a State Legislative Assembly, at a stage when disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution are pending or reasonably imminent against such member, shall not ipso facto terminate or render infructuous such disqualification proceedings, and that the Speaker/Chairman shall record a reasoned order, based on objective material, on both the voluntariness and genuineness of the resignation and on the disqualification petition,” the plea said. The plea sought direction to Speakers and Chairpersons to examine the voluntariness and genuineness of resignations on the basis of objective material and pass reasoned orders, while ensuring that pending disqualification proceedings are independently adjudicated.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: law / court / Election Commission of India / law enforcement

articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government Minister said, as her plans to come home in December 2026 fuel political tension and renewed street violence. Dhaka is instead seeking Ms. Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters. India’s External Affairs Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April 2026, the Ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s request to extradite Ms. Hasina. Ms. Hasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh, and her Awami League party is banned following the 2024 uprising that ended her long rule. The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest. Ms. Hasina fled Dhaka in August 2024 as protests demanding her resignation swept the country. She has since sought a new passport and identity card ahead of a planned return in December, requests the government has rejected. “As soon as she tries to enter Bangladesh, she will be arrested. And she will be taken to jail, and the law will take its course,” Ms. Obaed said in an interview on Sunday (November 22, 2026). “We would like India to honour the extradition treaty and return her as a convict, and the law will take its course. She (Ms. Hasina) will have to face the music.” The standoff has brought Ms. Hasina’s Awami League supporters out on the streets. The party this month announced a week of protests and rallies in support of Ms. Hasina’s return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19, 2026. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of arson targeting vehicles in at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, with several police officers and civilians injured, according to local media. Ms. Obaed called the violence a survival tactic by Ms. Hasina’s “politically bankrupt political party.” Khalid Mahmud Chowdhury, a senior Awami League official, said the current political establishment was responsible for the violence.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Minister said there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring Ms. Hasina back, adding that Dhaka wanted balanced ties with New Delhi that did not compromise Bangladesh’s “dignity, self-respect and interests.” “India needs to decide what kind of foreign policy they need to adopt for Bangladesh,” Ms. Obaed said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 04:05:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government Minister said, as her plans to come home in December 2026 fuel political tension and renewed street violence. Dhaka is instead seeking Ms. Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters. India’s External Affairs Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April 2026, the Ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s request to extradite Ms. Hasina. Ms. Hasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh, and her Awami League party is banned following the 2024 uprising that ended her long rule. The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest. Ms. Hasina fled Dhaka in August 2024 as protests demanding her resignation swept the country. She has since sought a new passport and identity card ahead of a planned return in December, requests the government has rejected. “As soon as she tries to enter Bangladesh, she will be arrested. And she will be taken to jail, and the law will take its course,” Ms. Obaed said in an interview on Sunday (November 22, 2026). “We would like India to honour the extradition treaty and return her as a convict, and the law will take its course. She (Ms. Hasina) will have to face the music.” The standoff has brought Ms. Hasina’s Awami League supporters out on the streets. The party this month announced a week of protests and rallies in support of Ms. Hasina’s return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19, 2026. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of arson targeting vehicles in at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, with several police officers and civilians injured, according to local media. Ms. Obaed called the violence a survival tactic by Ms. Hasina’s “politically bankrupt political party.” Khalid Mahmud Chowdhury, a senior Awami League official, said the current political establishment was responsible for the violence.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Minister said there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring Ms. Hasina back, adding that Dhaka wanted balanced ties with New Delhi that did not compromise Bangladesh’s “dignity, self-respect and interests.” “India needs to decide what kind of foreign policy they need to adopt for Bangladesh,” Ms. Obaed said.

स्थापना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Establishment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Extradition (Noun)
प्रत्यर्पण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Extradition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Resignation (Noun)
इस्तीफा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Resignation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Political (Adjective)
राजनीतिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Political' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Israel at an Inflection Point
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three years after Hamas’s October 7 attack shattered the core security promise of the state, Israel has emerged from a consequential Knesset election that ended Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing majority. Israel at an Inflection Point , published by The Hindu Group , examines how decades of unchecked militarism, a rightward political shift, and the collapse of the peace process have brought the country to this critical juncture. The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation. Tracing the arc from late-19th-century European Zionism and the 1948 establishment of Israel to the geopolitical shocks of 2026, it probes the central tension between military dominance and durable security. Across its chapters, the book explores how post-October 7 trauma has hardened Israeli opposition to Palestinian statehood, why tactical battlefield successes and high-profile assassinations have failed to produce a decisive strategic victory, and how rising American public scepticism and regional realignments are testing Washington’s traditionally unconditional backing. It also unpacks New Delhi’s pragmatic “de-hyphenation” policy, as India deepens defence and economic ties with Tel Aviv while maintaining its institutional support for a two-state solution. For readers seeking a deeper grasp of a rapidly shifting West Asia, Israel at an Inflection Point provides essential historical depth and geopolitical context. Read this e-book to examine the domestic fault lines reshaping Israeli polity, the global economic fallout of the conflict with Iran, and India’s delicate diplomatic balancing act in the region. · The predicament of the state of Israel by Stanly Johny · How Israel sees the Palestine question today by Sujata Ashwarya · From Gaza to Iran: Israel’s forever wars since October 7 by Rajeev Agarwal · The evolving dynamics of the U.S.–Israel special partnership by M.H. Ilias · Changes and continuity in India–Israel relations by Bashir Ali Abbas
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To download a sample of the e-book: https://newsth.live/Israel_ebook_sample

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Israel at an Inflection Point

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 02:50:37 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three years after Hamas’s October 7 attack shattered the core security promise of the state, Israel has emerged from a consequential Knesset election that ended Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing majority. Israel at an Inflection Point , published by The Hindu Group , examines how decades of unchecked militarism, a rightward political shift, and the collapse of the peace process have brought the country to this critical juncture. The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation. Tracing the arc from late-19th-century European Zionism and the 1948 establishment of Israel to the geopolitical shocks of 2026, it probes the central tension between military dominance and durable security. Across its chapters, the book explores how post-October 7 trauma has hardened Israeli opposition to Palestinian statehood, why tactical battlefield successes and high-profile assassinations have failed to produce a decisive strategic victory, and how rising American public scepticism and regional realignments are testing Washington’s traditionally unconditional backing. It also unpacks New Delhi’s pragmatic “de-hyphenation” policy, as India deepens defence and economic ties with Tel Aviv while maintaining its institutional support for a two-state solution. For readers seeking a deeper grasp of a rapidly shifting West Asia, Israel at an Inflection Point provides essential historical depth and geopolitical context. Read this e-book to examine the domestic fault lines reshaping Israeli polity, the global economic fallout of the conflict with Iran, and India’s delicate diplomatic balancing act in the region. · The predicament of the state of Israel by Stanly Johny · How Israel sees the Palestine question today by Sujata Ashwarya · From Gaza to Iran: Israel’s forever wars since October 7 by Rajeev Agarwal · The evolving dynamics of the U.S.–Israel special partnership by M.H. Ilias · Changes and continuity in India–Israel relations by Bashir Ali Abbas

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To download a sample of the e-book: https://newsth.live/Israel_ebook_sample

जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना।
✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।

व्यावहारिक और धरातलीय — सिर्फ किताबी सिद्धांतों के बजाय ज़मीनी हकीकत और नतीजों पर काम करने वाला।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Consequential' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: How did the COP31 climate agreement fall apart – and what happens now?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two days after the COP31 global climate summit was supposed to finish, the talks in Antalya, Turkey, have come to an end – but not as we might have hoped. Agreement simply could not be reached. The sticking point was the omission of fossil fuels in draft texts. The European Union led a revolt , shattering the consensus needed to adopt the cover text proposed by the Turkish and Australian conveners. In a year of unprecedented climate disasters , a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming , the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment . Some coverage has suggested the rejection of the cover text is a sign the entire summit was a failure. This isn’t quite right. These texts have always been add-ons to the formal negotiation process. Countries have regularly agreed these political, overarching statements, particularly since the Glasgow meeting in 2021, but they are not a requirement. Its failure does not signal the end of the COP process – or the breakdown of the Paris Agreement. What it may mean is that international climate cooperation will look different from this point onwards. For many observers, the litmus test for success at COP31 was whether countries could make any headway on the root cause of climate change – fossil fuels. Unfortunately, fossil fuels proved unmentionable. Three years ago at COP28 in Dubai, countries agreed to “ transition away from fossil fuels ”, marking the first time fossil fuels had explicitly been mentioned in an official decision text in decades of negotiations. The Dubai text was hailed as “ the beginning of the end of the fossil fuel era ”. But there was little sign that hope would be realised in Turkey.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a repeat of last year’s fraught negotiations at COP30 in Brazil, major fossil fuel producing nations Saudi Arabia and Russia banded together to block any reference in the negotiating outcomes and proposed cover text.

articles.title: How to tune into world radio music from a single app
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Whether you’re yearning for futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a North Korean curation of classical symphonies, or just the sound of your own mother tongue, Radio Garden is a fantastic tool for listeners of all ages

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If you listen to the radio while driving to work or doing the dishes, you’re probably familiar with five or so stations and regularly toggle between them in order to escape the ads. But imagine if you could point at almost any place on the map and tune into their radio offerings in real time. This is the premise of Radio Garden, which, in its own words, invites users to explore live radio around the world. The process is simple: open the Radio Garden app or website to get to a Google Earth -like interface sprinkled with green dots, pick a radio station you’re interested in, and wait for it to load. If the station is available and responsive, you’ll soon be tuning into what locals are listening to. Within a few minutes, a listener can explore futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a French curation of classical pieces, or the sound of their mother tongue as they imagine millions of others going about their day. A screengrab of the Radio Garden user interface on web | Photo Credit: Radio Garden Radio Garden has something for listeners of every age. Users can explore multiple available stations from the same place, or tour different cities. The local time is shown for each location, helping you get a sense of the kind of music you might hear there. The Google Earth-inspired interface is a fantastic way to introduce children to geography and the concept of time zones, as well as expose them to new cultures and languages through music . It can also aid in learning languages through immersion. The listening experience on Radio Garden is always unexpected; we enjoyed Chinese traffic updates and Columbian tunes for a while and were later surprised to hear a Pakistani radio station playing a popular Bollywood song . A Cairo radio station gently awakened sleepy listeners at sunrise with soothing romantic songs, while one in Pyongyang at the same time kept up post-lunch morale with fast-paced group duets. Radio Garden also offers curated playlists from stations all over the world for those who prefer a more thematic and cohesive listening experience, regardless of whether they lean more towards religious chants or rock songs. Furthermore, a fun ‘balloon ride’ game in Radio Garden randomly drops the listener right into a new place and starts playing the local radio station. It then slowly increases the viewer’s altitude to reveal more of the map, even as one races to guess which country’s music they are listening to.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The free version of Radio Garden comes with full-page visual ads that can be closed after a few seconds. We did not encounter any audio-based ads that interrupted our listening sessions, which is a major plus.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 How to tune into world radio music from a single app

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 02:44:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Whether you’re yearning for futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a North Korean curation of classical symphonies, or just the sound of your own mother tongue, Radio Garden is a fantastic tool for listeners of all ages

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If you listen to the radio while driving to work or doing the dishes, you’re probably familiar with five or so stations and regularly toggle between them in order to escape the ads. But imagine if you could point at almost any place on the map and tune into their radio offerings in real time. This is the premise of Radio Garden, which, in its own words, invites users to explore live radio around the world. The process is simple: open the Radio Garden app or website to get to a Google Earth -like interface sprinkled with green dots, pick a radio station you’re interested in, and wait for it to load. If the station is available and responsive, you’ll soon be tuning into what locals are listening to. Within a few minutes, a listener can explore futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a French curation of classical pieces, or the sound of their mother tongue as they imagine millions of others going about their day. A screengrab of the Radio Garden user interface on web | Photo Credit: Radio Garden Radio Garden has something for listeners of every age. Users can explore multiple available stations from the same place, or tour different cities. The local time is shown for each location, helping you get a sense of the kind of music you might hear there. The Google Earth-inspired interface is a fantastic way to introduce children to geography and the concept of time zones, as well as expose them to new cultures and languages through music . It can also aid in learning languages through immersion. The listening experience on Radio Garden is always unexpected; we enjoyed Chinese traffic updates and Columbian tunes for a while and were later surprised to hear a Pakistani radio station playing a popular Bollywood song . A Cairo radio station gently awakened sleepy listeners at sunrise with soothing romantic songs, while one in Pyongyang at the same time kept up post-lunch morale with fast-paced group duets. Radio Garden also offers curated playlists from stations all over the world for those who prefer a more thematic and cohesive listening experience, regardless of whether they lean more towards religious chants or rock songs. Furthermore, a fun ‘balloon ride’ game in Radio Garden randomly drops the listener right into a new place and starts playing the local radio station. It then slowly increases the viewer’s altitude to reveal more of the map, even as one races to guess which country’s music they are listening to.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The free version of Radio Garden comes with full-page visual ads that can be closed after a few seconds. We did not encounter any audio-based ads that interrupted our listening sessions, which is a major plus.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Experience (Noun)
अनुभव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Experience' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Classical (Adjective)
क्लासिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Classical' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: In search of skin lightening creams, kidneys take a hit
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Researchers from Kerala have reported a series of cases from Malappuram district where the regular use of fairness creams has been linked to nephrotic syndrome. Heavy metal screening of the blood and urine samples of these patients revealed high levels of mercury, the toxic effects of which are well-known

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On the heels of recent news reports on how keratin-based hair-straightening products containing glycolic acid derivatives led to severe kidney injury in women, researchers from Kerala have reported a series of cases wherein, the use of fairness creams has been linked to nephrotic syndrome. In a study published in the latest issue of Kidney International (‘NELL-1 associated membranous nephropathy linked to skin fairness cream use — insights from an Indian case series’, ) doctors describe a series of 15 cases of Membranous Nephropathy, reported by Aster MIMS Hospital, Kottakkal, Malappuram district, that were traced to the regular use of fairness creams. Heavy metal screening of the blood and urine samples of these patients revealed high levels of mercury, the toxic effects of which are well-known. An analysis of the fairness creams also showed that these contained high levels of mercury -- in some instances, 10,000 times above the permissible limit of 1 ppm.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Since 2021, Ranjith Narayanan, a nephrologist practising at two busy private hospitals in Kozhikode, had noticed a specific pattern in cases of membranous nephropathy diagnosed amongst his patients. They all had non-specific symptoms — fatigue, mild edema and frothy urine — but high levels of proteinuria, in the range of 6.5-22.2 g/day.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.
