🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 01:12:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. ✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Street plays to promote co-existence between humans and wildlife organised in Kotagiri
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Street plays to promote peaceful co-existence between humans and wildlife were organised in Kotagiri and Kattabettu forest ranges in the Nilgiris forest divisions recently.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The street plays were organised by Keystone Foundation in collaboration with the Forest Department. The two-day human-wildlife interaction awareness programme included street plays performed by Aayudham Foundation, Coimbatore, which ‘presented a series of engaging street plays to raise awareness among local communities about reducing negative interactions between humans and wildlife,’ a press release stated. The performances focused on the importance of peaceful coexistence with wildlife, particularly species such as sloth bears, leopards, tigers and elephants and practices that can be adopted by human communities to minimise negative interactions with wildlife. Key themes of the plays included understanding wildlife behaviour, avoiding encounters with wild animals, responsible waste disposal and the role of improper waste management in attracting wildlife towards human settlements. Through interactive and culturally engaging performances, the street plays highlighted how everyday human activities can influence wildlife movement and contribute to human–wildlife conflict. The programme also encouraged villagers to adopt responsible practices, remain alert and work collectively towards creating safer environments for both people and wildlife, the release added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A total of six street plays were conducted across the two forest ranges. Through the medium of street theatre, the initiative aimed to strengthen community awareness, encourage responsible behaviour and promote harmonious coexistence between local communities and wildlife, it added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Street plays to promote co-existence between humans and wildlife organised in Kotagiri

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:30:01 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Street plays to promote peaceful co-existence between humans and wildlife were organised in Kotagiri and Kattabettu forest ranges in the Nilgiris forest divisions recently.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The street plays were organised by Keystone Foundation in collaboration with the Forest Department. The two-day human-wildlife interaction awareness programme included street plays performed by Aayudham Foundation, Coimbatore, which ‘presented a series of engaging street plays to raise awareness among local communities about reducing negative interactions between humans and wildlife,’ a press release stated. The performances focused on the importance of peaceful coexistence with wildlife, particularly species such as sloth bears, leopards, tigers and elephants and practices that can be adopted by human communities to minimise negative interactions with wildlife. Key themes of the plays included understanding wildlife behaviour, avoiding encounters with wild animals, responsible waste disposal and the role of improper waste management in attracting wildlife towards human settlements. Through interactive and culturally engaging performances, the street plays highlighted how everyday human activities can influence wildlife movement and contribute to human–wildlife conflict. The programme also encouraged villagers to adopt responsible practices, remain alert and work collectively towards creating safer environments for both people and wildlife, the release added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A total of six street plays were conducted across the two forest ranges. Through the medium of street theatre, the initiative aimed to strengthen community awareness, encourage responsible behaviour and promote harmonious coexistence between local communities and wildlife, it added.

articles.title: Karnataka Ministers, MLAs should stay in farmers’ homes during Belagavi legislature session to cut costs: Farmers’ outfit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations said it was concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations has offered to arrange accommodation in farmers’ homes for Ministers, legislators and officials during the upcoming Legislature session in Belagavi as part of an effort to reduce government expenditure. Federation president Kurubur Shanthakumar has made the offer in an appeal addressed to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the presiding officers of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and the leaders of the Congress, BJP and JD(S) legislature parties. Mr. Shanthakumar has suggested that Ministers, MLAs and officials stay in farmers’ homes instead of hotels during the session, citing the financial constraints faced by the State Government in implementing its welfare schemes. He said farmers were concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought. “Although we are not in a position to provide financial assistance for the implementation of government schemes during these difficult times, we are capable of extending moral support. With this in mind, we, the farmers, have decided to extend our support to the MLAs and officials during this year’s Belagavi session,” he said. Pointing out that the government spends substantial amounts on hotel accommodation and other facilities for legislators and officials during every session, Mr. Shanthakumar appealed for a reduction in such expenditure. “We invite Ministers, MLAs, officials and government employees to stay in the homes of farming families instead of hotels,” he said. Hundreds of farming families were ready to host the elected representatives and officials, and the farmers themselves would bear the expenses of their hospitality, including food and other arrangements, he said. “This would help the government save the substantial amounts otherwise spent on hotel accommodation and preserve those funds in the State exchequer. Staying in farmers’ homes would also enable legislators to understand their problems first-hand and facilitate meaningful discussions during the Assembly session, paving the way for appropriate solutions,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Shanthakumar also suggested that the Legislature conduct proceedings over the weekends instead of allowing legislators to return to their respective hometowns. He proposed extending the daily sitting by two hours to make the session more productive and reduce additional expenditure.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Karnataka Ministers, MLAs should stay in farmers’ homes during Belagavi legislature session to cut costs: Farmers’ outfit

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:27:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations said it was concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations has offered to arrange accommodation in farmers’ homes for Ministers, legislators and officials during the upcoming Legislature session in Belagavi as part of an effort to reduce government expenditure. Federation president Kurubur Shanthakumar has made the offer in an appeal addressed to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the presiding officers of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and the leaders of the Congress, BJP and JD(S) legislature parties. Mr. Shanthakumar has suggested that Ministers, MLAs and officials stay in farmers’ homes instead of hotels during the session, citing the financial constraints faced by the State Government in implementing its welfare schemes. He said farmers were concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought. “Although we are not in a position to provide financial assistance for the implementation of government schemes during these difficult times, we are capable of extending moral support. With this in mind, we, the farmers, have decided to extend our support to the MLAs and officials during this year’s Belagavi session,” he said. Pointing out that the government spends substantial amounts on hotel accommodation and other facilities for legislators and officials during every session, Mr. Shanthakumar appealed for a reduction in such expenditure. “We invite Ministers, MLAs, officials and government employees to stay in the homes of farming families instead of hotels,” he said. Hundreds of farming families were ready to host the elected representatives and officials, and the farmers themselves would bear the expenses of their hospitality, including food and other arrangements, he said. “This would help the government save the substantial amounts otherwise spent on hotel accommodation and preserve those funds in the State exchequer. Staying in farmers’ homes would also enable legislators to understand their problems first-hand and facilitate meaningful discussions during the Assembly session, paving the way for appropriate solutions,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Shanthakumar also suggested that the Legislature conduct proceedings over the weekends instead of allowing legislators to return to their respective hometowns. He proposed extending the daily sitting by two hours to make the session more productive and reduce additional expenditure.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations said it was concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Federation of Karnataka Farmers’ Organisations has offered to arrange accommodation in farmers’ homes for Ministers, legislators and officials during the upcoming Legislature session in Belagavi as part of an effort to reduce government expenditure. Federation president Kurubur Shanthakumar has made the offer in an appeal addressed to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the presiding officers of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and the leaders of the Congress, BJP and JD(S) legislature parties. Mr. Shanthakumar has suggested that Ministers, MLAs and officials stay in farmers’ homes instead of hotels during the session, citing the financial constraints faced by the State Government in implementing its welfare schemes. He said farmers were concerned about the State government’s financial position, particularly as it was convening a special session of the Legislature against the backdrop of the prevailing drought. “Although we are not in a position to provide financial assistance for the implementation of government schemes during these difficult times, we are capable of extending moral support. With this in mind, we, the farmers, have decided to extend our support to the MLAs and officials during this year’s Belagavi session,” he said. Pointing out that the government spends substantial amounts on hotel accommodation and other facilities for legislators and officials during every session, Mr. Shanthakumar appealed for a reduction in such expenditure. “We invite Ministers, MLAs, officials and government employees to stay in the homes of farming families instead of hotels,” he said. Hundreds of farming families were ready to host the elected representatives and officials, and the farmers themselves would bear the expenses of their hospitality, including food and other arrangements, he said. “This would help the government save the substantial amounts otherwise spent on hotel accommodation and preserve those funds in the State exchequer. Staying in farmers’ homes would also enable legislators to understand their problems first-hand and facilitate meaningful discussions during the Assembly session, paving the way for appropriate solutions,” he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Shanthakumar also suggested that the Legislature conduct proceedings over the weekends instead of allowing legislators to return to their respective hometowns. He proposed extending the daily sitting by two hours to make the session more productive and reduce additional expenditure.

articles.title: Two men found murdered in separate incidents in Tumakuru district; police suspect personal enmity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In both incidents, the victims were attacked with a sharp weapon

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two men were murdered in separate incidents in Tumakuru district, with both victims suffering fatal head injuries inflicted with heavy weapons, police said on Monday (November 23, 2026). In the first incident, a 35-year-old factory worker was murdered while sleeping outside his house at Jakkenahalli village, within the limits of Tumakuru Rural police station. The victim, identified as Mutthuraj, was sleeping in front of his house when unidentified assailants allegedly attacked him with a heavy weapon on the head around midnight on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Superintendent in-charge of Tumakuru district C. Gopal told reporters that the police received information about the murder around 6 a.m. on November 23 after the victim’s sister noticed the incident and alerted neighbours. In a separate incident, an unidentified man was found murdered near a bridge at Cheelaganahalli, within the limits of Koratagere police station, on Saturday (November 21) morning. The body was found about 1.5 km before the village, near a bridge. The victim had sustained severe head injuries, apparently inflicted with a sharp weapon. Gopal said the police received information around 7 a.m. after people travelling along the route noticed the body and alerted the police. “Prima facie, the deceased appears to be from North India. He may have been working at a factory or elsewhere in the region. We suspect he could have been assaulted at another location following an altercation and his body dumped near the bridge. However, this is only a preliminary assessment,” he said. The police are yet to establish the identity of the deceased. Efforts are being made to identify him through all available investigative methods.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Police are also examining CCTV footage and gathering information from various sources to identify and trace the assailants in both cases.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Two men found murdered in separate incidents in Tumakuru district; police suspect personal enmity

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:26:52 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In both incidents, the victims were attacked with a sharp weapon

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two men were murdered in separate incidents in Tumakuru district, with both victims suffering fatal head injuries inflicted with heavy weapons, police said on Monday (November 23, 2026). In the first incident, a 35-year-old factory worker was murdered while sleeping outside his house at Jakkenahalli village, within the limits of Tumakuru Rural police station. The victim, identified as Mutthuraj, was sleeping in front of his house when unidentified assailants allegedly attacked him with a heavy weapon on the head around midnight on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Superintendent in-charge of Tumakuru district C. Gopal told reporters that the police received information about the murder around 6 a.m. on November 23 after the victim’s sister noticed the incident and alerted neighbours. In a separate incident, an unidentified man was found murdered near a bridge at Cheelaganahalli, within the limits of Koratagere police station, on Saturday (November 21) morning. The body was found about 1.5 km before the village, near a bridge. The victim had sustained severe head injuries, apparently inflicted with a sharp weapon. Gopal said the police received information around 7 a.m. after people travelling along the route noticed the body and alerted the police. “Prima facie, the deceased appears to be from North India. He may have been working at a factory or elsewhere in the region. We suspect he could have been assaulted at another location following an altercation and his body dumped near the bridge. However, this is only a preliminary assessment,” he said. The police are yet to establish the identity of the deceased. Efforts are being made to identify him through all available investigative methods.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Police are also examining CCTV footage and gathering information from various sources to identify and trace the assailants in both cases.

articles.title: Telangana govt seeks 12-month gap in crop loan repayment for farmers in drought-hit mandals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: An extension of 60-month in total repayment period sought for 111 severely affected mandals

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana Government has asked the banks to consider a 12-month moratorium and extension of total repayment period to 60 months for borrowers in the 111 mandals severely affected by drought across the State. Moratorium of 12 months and extension of total repayment period by 36 months should be considered for 254 moderately affected mandals . Banks were asked to identify eligible accounts on suo-motu basis to initiate available relief process without waiting for borrowers to approach them, through a suitable communication to the borrowers wherever deemed fit. The banks should also make available option for borrowers to opt out of the resolution plan at any point till the end of 135 days from the date of declaration of calamity on October 24. The State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC), which met under the chairmanship of Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, recently had resolved to sanction additional need-based finance to eligible affected farmers to address financial stress and restoration and continuation of productive activities. This will be subject to borrower wise viability assessment, projected cash flows and approved policies of the respective banks’ boards. It has also resolved to ensure that insurance proceeds, if any, should be adjusted towards the restructured accounts in cases where fresh loans have been granted to the borrowers. Banks could, however, consider restructuring and sanctioning fresh loans without waiting for the actual receipt of the claim.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SLBC has requested the State Government to take up with the Central Government the issue of extending interest subvention benefit in rescheduled crop loans affected by drought till the repayment term ends as it will benefit farmers.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Telangana govt seeks 12-month gap in crop loan repayment for farmers in drought-hit mandals

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:19:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: An extension of 60-month in total repayment period sought for 111 severely affected mandals

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana Government has asked the banks to consider a 12-month moratorium and extension of total repayment period to 60 months for borrowers in the 111 mandals severely affected by drought across the State. Moratorium of 12 months and extension of total repayment period by 36 months should be considered for 254 moderately affected mandals . Banks were asked to identify eligible accounts on suo-motu basis to initiate available relief process without waiting for borrowers to approach them, through a suitable communication to the borrowers wherever deemed fit. The banks should also make available option for borrowers to opt out of the resolution plan at any point till the end of 135 days from the date of declaration of calamity on October 24. The State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC), which met under the chairmanship of Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, recently had resolved to sanction additional need-based finance to eligible affected farmers to address financial stress and restoration and continuation of productive activities. This will be subject to borrower wise viability assessment, projected cash flows and approved policies of the respective banks’ boards. It has also resolved to ensure that insurance proceeds, if any, should be adjusted towards the restructured accounts in cases where fresh loans have been granted to the borrowers. Banks could, however, consider restructuring and sanctioning fresh loans without waiting for the actual receipt of the claim.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SLBC has requested the State Government to take up with the Central Government the issue of extending interest subvention benefit in rescheduled crop loans affected by drought till the repayment term ends as it will benefit farmers.

articles.title: India-Nepal weekly train: Check stations, timings and more about Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu-Kamala Express
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham Saryu-Kamala Express will have 10 stations, scheduled for departure every Monday. Check out for further details on stations and timings

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In a bid to boost connectivity and bilateral ties with Nepal, the Ministry of Railways has launched Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express . Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh to Janakpur in Nepal, from Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026). The weekly train will establish a crucial rail link between two pilgrimage sites, namely Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Sita and Ram. Further, the initiative is expected to enhance trade and cultural ties between both countries. The train will cover a distance of approximately 604 kilometres in 19 hours, passing through several important towns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh . The weekly train will commence its journey from Janakpur Dham on Saturday, and from Ayodhya Cantt on Monday. The express train will commence regular service from November 28. The originating train (15596) from India is scheduled to depart from its station at Ayodhya Cantt. at 5:50 p.m every Monday, and reach the final destination at Janakpur at 12:40 p.m. (Nepali time) next day. On its return journey, the train will leave Janakpur Dham at 1.10 pm (Nepali time) every Saturday and reach Ayodhya Cantt at 8.10 am on Sundays. The train is scheduled to halt at 10 stations as part of its itinerary. Here is the list of stations where the train will have stoppages besides its terminal stations. The Saryu-Kamala Express will be operated using modern 17-coach LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) rakes. The train configuration includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, one LSLRD (LHB Second Class, Luggage, Brake, and Disabled-friendly) coach, and one LWLRRM (LHB Power Car/Generator-cum-Luggage-cum-Brake Van) coach. The ticket prices for the Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express are yet to be announced on the IRCTC website. Indian citizens going to Nepal don’t need a visa if they have a valid passport. Train services from India are conducted to neighbouring countries of Bangladesh and Nepal.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Nepal / travel and commuting / railway / Bihar / Uttar Pradesh

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 India-Nepal weekly train: Check stations, timings and more about Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu-Kamala Express

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:16:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham Saryu-Kamala Express will have 10 stations, scheduled for departure every Monday. Check out for further details on stations and timings

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In a bid to boost connectivity and bilateral ties with Nepal, the Ministry of Railways has launched Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express . Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh to Janakpur in Nepal, from Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026). The weekly train will establish a crucial rail link between two pilgrimage sites, namely Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Sita and Ram. Further, the initiative is expected to enhance trade and cultural ties between both countries. The train will cover a distance of approximately 604 kilometres in 19 hours, passing through several important towns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh . The weekly train will commence its journey from Janakpur Dham on Saturday, and from Ayodhya Cantt on Monday. The express train will commence regular service from November 28. The originating train (15596) from India is scheduled to depart from its station at Ayodhya Cantt. at 5:50 p.m every Monday, and reach the final destination at Janakpur at 12:40 p.m. (Nepali time) next day. On its return journey, the train will leave Janakpur Dham at 1.10 pm (Nepali time) every Saturday and reach Ayodhya Cantt at 8.10 am on Sundays. The train is scheduled to halt at 10 stations as part of its itinerary. Here is the list of stations where the train will have stoppages besides its terminal stations. The Saryu-Kamala Express will be operated using modern 17-coach LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) rakes. The train configuration includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, one LSLRD (LHB Second Class, Luggage, Brake, and Disabled-friendly) coach, and one LWLRRM (LHB Power Car/Generator-cum-Luggage-cum-Brake Van) coach. The ticket prices for the Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express are yet to be announced on the IRCTC website. Indian citizens going to Nepal don’t need a visa if they have a valid passport. Train services from India are conducted to neighbouring countries of Bangladesh and Nepal.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Nepal / travel and commuting / railway / Bihar / Uttar Pradesh

द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way

विन्यास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Configuration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

कनेक्टिविटी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Connectivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Destination (Adjective / Verb)
गंतव्य — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Destination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay. Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings. Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs. Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand. “Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said. The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest. A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions. There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives. Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भोजन, आवास और परिवहन लागत में बढ़ोतरी का हवाला देते हुए श्रमिक न्यूनतम मासिक वेतन 12,500 टका से बढ़ाकर 30,000 टका ($242) करने की मांग कर रहे हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उद्योग जगत के नेताओं ने कहा कि बांग्लादेश के कपड़ा निर्माता सोमवार (23 सितंबर, 2026) को अधिकारियों के साथ बातचीत में न्यूनतम मासिक वेतन में लगभग 15% की वृद्धि का प्रस्ताव कर सकते हैं, जो श्रमिकों की उनके वेतन को दोगुना से अधिक करने की मांग से काफी कम है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — नवंबर की शुरुआत से, वेतन को लेकर अशांति के कारण दुनिया के दूसरे सबसे बड़े परिधान निर्यातक में शटडाउन और हिंसा हुई है, जो 4 मिलियन से अधिक श्रमिकों को रोजगार देता है और एच एंड एम, गैप और वॉलमार्ट सहित प्रमुख वैश्विक खुदरा विक्रेताओं के लिए आपूर्ति प्रदान करता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — वेतन को लेकर विरोध उस उद्योग के लागत लाभ का परीक्षण कर रहा है जो देश की 80% से अधिक निर्यात आय उत्पन्न करता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — भोजन, आवास और परिवहन लागत में बढ़ोतरी का हवाला देते हुए श्रमिक न्यूनतम मासिक वेतन 12,500 टका से बढ़ाकर 30,000 टका ($242) करने की मांग कर रहे हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उद्योग के नेताओं, जिन्होंने मुद्दे की संवेदनशीलता के कारण नाम न छापने की शर्त पर रॉयटर्स से बात की, ने कहा कि 15% से अधिक की वृद्धि टिकाऊ नहीं होगी क्योंकि क्षेत्र बढ़ती लागत और कमजोर वैश्विक मांग से जूझ रहा है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Sensitivity' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवेदनशीलता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Sensitivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: “Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उद्योग जगत के एक नेता ने कहा, "फिर भी, कई छोटी फ़ैक्टरियाँ वृद्धि से निपटने के लिए संघर्ष कर सकती हैं।"।

hinglishTracks.en: The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अशांति से उद्योग को काफी नुकसान हुआ है।।

hinglishTracks.en: A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — बांग्लादेश गारमेंट मैन्युफैक्चरर्स एंड एक्सपोर्टर्स एसोसिएशन के एक सर्वेक्षण में पाया गया कि 18 दिनों के व्यवधान के कारण 317 कारखानों में लगभग 428 मिलियन डॉलर का नुकसान हुआ, जबकि अंतरराष्ट्रीय खरीदारों ने उत्पादन में व्यवधान पर चिंताओं के बीच लगभग 254 मिलियन डॉलर के ऑर्डर अन्य देशों में स्थानांतरित कर दिए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — श्रम मंत्री या श्रमिकों के प्रतिनिधियों की ओर से तत्काल कोई टिप्पणी नहीं आई।।

hinglishTracks.en: Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उद्योग के नेताओं ने कहा कि उच्च उत्पादन लागत, बढ़ती उपयोगिता शुल्क और प्रतिद्वंद्वी परिधान उत्पादक देशों से तीव्र प्रतिस्पर्धा निर्माताओं की काफी बड़ी वेतन वृद्धि को अवशोषित करने की क्षमता को सीमित करती है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Competition' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रतियोगिता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Competition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:44:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay. Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings. Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs. Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand. “Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said. The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest. A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions. There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives. Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Sensitivity (Noun)
संवेदनशीलता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Sensitivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Association (Noun)
संगठन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Association' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Competition (Noun)
प्रतियोगिता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Competition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs." (Hinglish Arth: भोजन, आवास और परिवहन लागत में बढ़ोतरी का हवाला देते हुए श्रमिक न्यूनतम मासिक वेतन 12,500 टका से बढ़ाकर 30,000 टका ($242) करने की मांग कर रहे हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and..." (Hinglish Arth: इस महीने की शुरुआत में शुरू हुए विरोध प्रदर्शनों ने सैकड़ों कारखानों को बंद करने के लिए मजबूर किया और श्रमिकों और पुलिस के बीच झड़पें हुईं, जिन्होंने प्रदर्शनकारियों को तितर-बितर करने के लिए आंसू गैस और ध्वनि ग्रेनेड का इस्तेमाल किया।)

articles.title: China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals. "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians. “We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas. Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair attracts businessmen from around the world to showcase their businesses to Chinese consumers. Beijing has also stopped the service provider China Visa Application Centre from accepting visa applications, and its missions have begun handling them directly amid rising demand for Chinese visas, especially business visas. The visa process between the two countries improved after India began issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years, amid efforts to repair bilateral ties that came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties. With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals. "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians. “We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas. Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties. With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals. "China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians. “We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said. The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas. Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair attracts businessmen from around the world to showcase their businesses to Chinese consumers. Beijing has also stopped the service provider China Visa Application Centre from accepting visa applications, and its missions have begun handling them directly amid rising demand for Chinese visas, especially business visas. The visa process between the two countries improved after India began issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years, amid efforts to repair bilateral ties that came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties. With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

articles.title: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warns of possible misuse of WhatsApp Web sessions
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit issues advisory asking users to manually log out after every session

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, has warned WhatsApp users about the possible misuse of authenticated web sessions to gain unauthorised access to their accounts. In an advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of the I4C said a malicious person could exploit an active WhatsApp Web session to read private messages, send messages by impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and misuse the user’s trusted identity for fraud, phishing and other cybercrimes. The unit has asked users to exercise caution while accessing WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices that may be accessible to others. It recommended users to avoid exchanging government-related, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web mode on computers. Users have also been advised against keeping their accounts permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session. Simply closing the browser window or tab should not be considered sufficient to terminate an authenticated session, the advisory said. Where using WhatsApp Web was unavoidable, the users were advised to opt for ‘Incognito’ or ‘Private Browsing’ mode on trusted computers and log out manually before closing the browser. Logging in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres and borrowed or otherwise untrusted systems should be avoided. The unit also urged WhatsApp users to remain alert to unusual account activity. Unexpected messages sent from user accounts or unexplained replies from contacts should be viewed seriously. The advisory called for keeping operating systems, browsers and security software updated. Users were advised to avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files and untrusted software.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Institutions or organisations were advised to avoid using WhatsApp Web in official and sensitive work environments.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre warns of possible misuse of WhatsApp Web sessions

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 05:12:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit issues advisory asking users to manually log out after every session

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, has warned WhatsApp users about the possible misuse of authenticated web sessions to gain unauthorised access to their accounts. In an advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of the I4C said a malicious person could exploit an active WhatsApp Web session to read private messages, send messages by impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and misuse the user’s trusted identity for fraud, phishing and other cybercrimes. The unit has asked users to exercise caution while accessing WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices that may be accessible to others. It recommended users to avoid exchanging government-related, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web mode on computers. Users have also been advised against keeping their accounts permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session. Simply closing the browser window or tab should not be considered sufficient to terminate an authenticated session, the advisory said. Where using WhatsApp Web was unavoidable, the users were advised to opt for ‘Incognito’ or ‘Private Browsing’ mode on trusted computers and log out manually before closing the browser. Logging in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres and borrowed or otherwise untrusted systems should be avoided. The unit also urged WhatsApp users to remain alert to unusual account activity. Unexpected messages sent from user accounts or unexplained replies from contacts should be viewed seriously. The advisory called for keeping operating systems, browsers and security software updated. Users were advised to avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files and untrusted software.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Institutions or organisations were advised to avoid using WhatsApp Web in official and sensitive work environments.

articles.title: No cluster kitchens for midday meals in Karnataka, says Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Minister says that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has assured that cluster kitchens (centralised cooking facilities) will not be established under the scheme providing midday meals to schoolchildren (Classes I to X) in the State. He said that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs. On Monday, S. Balan, honorary president of Akshara Dasoha (Midday Meal Workers’ Union), met the Minister at his residence and submitted a list of demands, including not entertaining the idea of cluster kitchens. The delegation also sought a hike in monthly remuneration, citing the example of Keralam, where workers are paid ₹12,000, compared with ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 in Karnataka. Mr. Bangarappa said he would discuss the demand with the Chief Minister. “It is to our government’s credit that we previously raised the retirement corpus for midday meal workers to ₹40,000,” he said. He advised the union to meet Union government officials, noting that the midday meal scheme is not solely funded by the State government and involves participation from the Centre as well. Mr. Balan also raised concerns over substandard grains and rice being supplied to government schools to cook midday meals for children. The Minister sought precise details on where such incidents were occurring, promising strict action.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister outlining various demands, including the establishment of joint bank accounts for school headmasters and head cooks, a retirement corpus of at least ₹1 lakh, and a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 No cluster kitchens for midday meals in Karnataka, says Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:25:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Minister says that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has assured that cluster kitchens (centralised cooking facilities) will not be established under the scheme providing midday meals to schoolchildren (Classes I to X) in the State. He said that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs. On Monday, S. Balan, honorary president of Akshara Dasoha (Midday Meal Workers’ Union), met the Minister at his residence and submitted a list of demands, including not entertaining the idea of cluster kitchens. The delegation also sought a hike in monthly remuneration, citing the example of Keralam, where workers are paid ₹12,000, compared with ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 in Karnataka. Mr. Bangarappa said he would discuss the demand with the Chief Minister. “It is to our government’s credit that we previously raised the retirement corpus for midday meal workers to ₹40,000,” he said. He advised the union to meet Union government officials, noting that the midday meal scheme is not solely funded by the State government and involves participation from the Centre as well. Mr. Balan also raised concerns over substandard grains and rice being supplied to government schools to cook midday meals for children. The Minister sought precise details on where such incidents were occurring, promising strict action.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister outlining various demands, including the establishment of joint bank accounts for school headmasters and head cooks, a retirement corpus of at least ₹1 lakh, and a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।

पारिश्रमिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Remuneration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For at least three years, the personal data that voters submitted to the Election Commission of India through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on its Citizen Service Portal (https://voters.eci.gov.in/ ) to anyone with a login, claims a report by ‘Charchagram’, a civic-tech initiative for building tools for enhancing transparency and accountability in public systems of India. It said that while records going back to 2023 were verified for this report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer. According to the report, using ECI published data, it estimates that at least seven crore Form 6 enrolments took place in this period. Each Form 6 application holds a citizen’s name, their relative’s name, gender, phone number, email, home address, photograph, Aadhaar details, age-proof documents, and address-proof documents, among other details. “We audited the front-end code available in public. And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram. Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was. “The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report. Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In. CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:24:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For at least three years, the personal data that voters submitted to the Election Commission of India through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on its Citizen Service Portal (https://voters.eci.gov.in/ ) to anyone with a login, claims a report by ‘Charchagram’, a civic-tech initiative for building tools for enhancing transparency and accountability in public systems of India. It said that while records going back to 2023 were verified for this report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer. According to the report, using ECI published data, it estimates that at least seven crore Form 6 enrolments took place in this period. Each Form 6 application holds a citizen’s name, their relative’s name, gender, phone number, email, home address, photograph, Aadhaar details, age-proof documents, and address-proof documents, among other details. “We audited the front-end code available in public. And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram. Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was. “The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report. Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In. CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Predictably (Adverb)
जैसा पहले से अनुमान था — बिना किसी आश्चर्य के बिल्कुल पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक होना।
✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Acknowledgement (Adjective)
पावती — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Acknowledgement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 wa' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be..." (Hinglish Arth: हालाँकि रिपोर्ट के लिए 2023 से पहले के रिकॉर्ड सत्यापित किए गए थे, लेकिन ऐसा कुछ भी नहीं था जो बताता हो कि पहले के रिकॉर्ड सुरक्षित थे, इसलिए एक्सपोज़र लंबा हो सकता है)

A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr." (Hinglish Arth: श्रीमान ने कहा, "हमने सात दिनों के भीतर समाधान करने और ऐसा हो जाने पर लिखित पावती और पुष्टि के लिए कहा।")

articles.title: A.P. CM calls for wider use of AI in healthcare, agriculture to improve public services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chandrababu Naidu directs senior officials to take up capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has called for the wider application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across various sectors, including healthcare and agriculture, to improve service delivery, administrative efficiency and government revenue. Reviewing the functioning of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) with senior officials of various departments on Sunday, Mr. Naidu stressed the need to leverage modern technology and the AI stack to simplify government services and improve the performance of departments. He directed officials to take measures to ensure that public services were delivered more efficiently and promptly. He also called for capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees. Stressing that delays in addressing public grievances should be avoided, the Chief Minister has directed officials to expedite the resolution of complaints received through the Public Grievance Redressal System. A positive public perception of government services was essential for improving governance and called upon departments to regularly review their performance and address shortcomings in monitoring mechanisms, he said. Mr. Naidu said the government was using Revenue and Legal AI stacks to analyse various issues and identify ways to improve departmental performance. Data-driven decision-making would become increasingly important in governance in the coming years, he observed. Referring to the recent local body elections, he said the results could serve as one of the indicators of the government’s performance. He asked senior departmental officials to strengthen monitoring mechanisms and ensure better delivery of services to the public.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior officials from the Social Welfare, BC Welfare, Minority Welfare, Finance, Municipal Administration and Energy departments, besides RTGS officials, participated in the review meeting.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 A.P. CM calls for wider use of AI in healthcare, agriculture to improve public services

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 07:22:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Chandrababu Naidu directs senior officials to take up capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has called for the wider application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across various sectors, including healthcare and agriculture, to improve service delivery, administrative efficiency and government revenue. Reviewing the functioning of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) with senior officials of various departments on Sunday, Mr. Naidu stressed the need to leverage modern technology and the AI stack to simplify government services and improve the performance of departments. He directed officials to take measures to ensure that public services were delivered more efficiently and promptly. He also called for capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees. Stressing that delays in addressing public grievances should be avoided, the Chief Minister has directed officials to expedite the resolution of complaints received through the Public Grievance Redressal System. A positive public perception of government services was essential for improving governance and called upon departments to regularly review their performance and address shortcomings in monitoring mechanisms, he said. Mr. Naidu said the government was using Revenue and Legal AI stacks to analyse various issues and identify ways to improve departmental performance. Data-driven decision-making would become increasingly important in governance in the coming years, he observed. Referring to the recent local body elections, he said the results could serve as one of the indicators of the government’s performance. He asked senior departmental officials to strengthen monitoring mechanisms and ensure better delivery of services to the public.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior officials from the Social Welfare, BC Welfare, Minority Welfare, Finance, Municipal Administration and Energy departments, besides RTGS officials, participated in the review meeting.

articles.title: Government will explore all possible ways to avoid electricity restriction in Keralam, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Sunny Joseph announces that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government will explore all possible ways to avoid power restrictions in the State, Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has said. Addressing a Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) review meeting at Thodupuzha in Idukki on Monday, Joseph said that due to the El Niño effect, rainfall has been largely reduced in the State, affecting the storage levels of hydroelectric dams. “Compared to the previous year, the water level in Idukki, including major hydel dams, is more than 20% below storage this year. Presently, there is only 60% storage in the hydel dams in the State,” the Minister said. Mr. Joseph further noted that the government will t launch initiatives to arrange power from other sources. According to KSEB data, the water level in the Idukki dam on Monday was 2,368.9 feet (63%), compared with 2,384.98 feet (79%) on the same day last year. During the meeting, the Minister announced that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1. He said the decision was taken based on repeated demands from various quarters. The Minister also directed officials to take steps to resume the boating facility at the Anayirankal dam reservoir. Based on the recommendation of a panel appointed by the High Court to address human-animal conflicts in Chinnakkanal, the boating facility in Anayirankal was suspended following the court’s direction on July 14, 2023. The panel had argued that stopping the boating facility in Anayirankal would help prevent human-elephant conflicts in the Anayirankal and Chinnakkanal regions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Joseph further noted that to tap the tourism potential in Idukki, the KSEB and the Tourism department will jointly implement projects in the district. He also said the Electricity department will seek permission from the forest department to set up an overhead power line to Edamalakkudy, the State’s first tribal panchayat, to provide electricity to the tribal community.

Addressing a Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) review meeting at Thodupuzha in Idukki on Monday, Joseph said that due to the El Niño effect, rainfall has been largely reduced in the State, affecting the storage levels of hydroelectric dams. “Compared to the previous year, the water level in Idukki, including major hydel dams, is more than 20% below storage this year. Presently, there is only 60% storage in the hydel dams in the State,” the Minister said. Mr. Joseph further noted that the government will t launch initiatives to arrange power from other sources. According to KSEB data, the water level in the Idukki dam on Monday was 2,368.9 feet (63%), compared with 2,384.98 feet (79%) on the same day last year. During the meeting, the Minister announced that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1. He said the decision was taken based on repeated demands from various quarters. The Minister also directed officials to take steps to resume the boating facility at the Anayirankal dam reservoir. Based on the recommendation of a panel appointed by the High Court to address human-animal conflicts in Chinnakkanal, the boating facility in Anayirankal was suspended following the court’s direction on July 14, 2023. The panel had argued that stopping the boating facility in Anayirankal would help prevent human-elephant conflicts in the Anayirankal and Chinnakkanal regions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Joseph further noted that to tap the tourism potential in Idukki, the KSEB and the Tourism department will jointly implement projects in the district. He also said the Electricity department will seek permission from the forest department to set up an overhead power line to Edamalakkudy, the State’s first tribal panchayat, to provide electricity to the tribal community.
