🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 01:44:51 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

articles.title: Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses. While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns. Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said. With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added. Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

3. articles.deepExplanation:
1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses. While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns. Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said. With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added. Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 01:37:35 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses. While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns. Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said. With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added. Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

articles.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location. Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco. Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States". The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line. The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally." "Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Iran's demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:59:25 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location. Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco. Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States". The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line. The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally." "Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Iran's demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Delegation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on ​Saturday (November 21, 2026) despite heavy rain to protest against soaring living ‌costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages. Organiser ​CGTP, Portugal’s largest trade union federation, called ⁠for higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essential goods and services, and measures to curb housing costs. The ‌CGTP said turnout reached “many thousands” as protesters carrying umbrellas and wearing hooded ponchos marched ‌along two of Lisbon’s main avenues. Police ‌did ⁠not provide an estimate. “We work more, we ⁠have more expenses and we don’t have money for day-to-day life,” said Manuel Gomes, 44, a factory worker, arguing that the ​centre-right government’s policies ‌had made matters worse. Protestors demanding affordable housing and carrying a banner with the words "Fight for our future, not in their wars" walks past a Christmas market in downtown Lisbon, on November 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP “Our wages are low, diesel and gasoline prices keep going up, and so do housing costs and everything else. We have ‌to change this,” Gomes said. Portugal’s average annual earnings ​in 2025 were 37% below the European Union average, according to Eurostat. Inflation ⁠hit 3.8% in October, driven by food and energy prices amid continuing tensions in the Middle East. Portugal is ‌also grappling with one of Europe’s most severe housing affordability crises. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, hitting younger people particularly hard. Luis Russo (66), a retired IT technician, said he ‌was demonstrating to demand “higher wages and pensions and against speculation in ​the rental market”, accusing the government of serving “big interests” rather than ordinary people.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on ​Saturday (November 21, 2026) despite heavy rain to protest against soaring living ‌costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages. Organiser ​CGTP, Portugal’s largest trade union federation, called ⁠for higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essential goods and services, and measures to curb housing costs. The ‌CGTP said turnout reached “many thousands” as protesters carrying umbrellas and wearing hooded ponchos marched ‌along two of Lisbon’s main avenues. Police ‌did ⁠not provide an estimate. “We work more, we ⁠have more expenses and we don’t have money for day-to-day life,” said Manuel Gomes, 44, a factory worker, arguing that the ​centre-right government’s policies ‌had made matters worse. Protestors demanding affordable housing and carrying a banner with the words "Fight for our future, not in their wars" walks past a Christmas market in downtown Lisbon, on November 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP “Our wages are low, diesel and gasoline prices keep going up, and so do housing costs and everything else. We have ‌to change this,” Gomes said. Portugal’s average annual earnings ​in 2025 were 37% below the European Union average, according to Eurostat. Inflation ⁠hit 3.8% in October, driven by food and energy prices amid continuing tensions in the Middle East. Portugal is ‌also grappling with one of Europe’s most severe housing affordability crises. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, hitting younger people particularly hard. Luis Russo (66), a retired IT technician, said he ‌was demonstrating to demand “higher wages and pensions and against speculation in ​the rental market”, accusing the government of serving “big interests” rather than ordinary people.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026). articles.title: FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently. The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people. Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India. The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants. Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

articles.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). “For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said. Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”. It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:08:25 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). “For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said. Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”. It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administrative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administrative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Comprehensive (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Comprehensive' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displacement
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: T he International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s top court, on November 19, ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the military’s 2017 clearance operations in Rakhine State. This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide. The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods. In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution. Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation. Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled. Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region. The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces. And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical. While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya. Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013. The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years. Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017. Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017. Longing for justice: Rohingya refugees watch the live announcement of the verdict in a genocide case against Myanmar on November 19, 2026

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agony of loss: Hamida, a Rohingya refugee, weeps as she holds her 40-day-old son, who died after their boat capsized before reaching the shore in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on September 14, 2017.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — संयुक्त राष्ट्र की शीर्ष अदालत, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय (आईसीजे) ने 19 नवंबर को फैसला सुनाया कि म्यांमार ने रखाइन राज्य में सेना के 2017 निकासी अभियानों के दौरान रोहिंग्या अल्पसंख्यक के खिलाफ नरसंहार किया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — यह पहली बार था जब विश्व न्यायालय ने किसी देश को नरसंहार के लिए जिम्मेदार ठहराया।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — मुख्य रूप से मुस्लिम जातीय अल्पसंख्यक रोहिंग्या को दक्षिण पूर्व एशियाई देश में दशकों से व्यवस्थित भेदभाव का सामना करना पड़ा है, जिसमें नागरिकता से इनकार, आंदोलन और शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल और आजीविका तक पहुंच पर प्रतिबंध शामिल है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Discrimination' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Discrimination' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — अगस्त 2017 में, सामूहिक हत्याओं, यौन हिंसा और गांवों को जलाने से जुड़ी एक सैन्य कार्रवाई ने 7,40,000 से अधिक रोहिंग्या को पड़ोसी बांग्लादेश में भागने के लिए मजबूर कर दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — वे शरणार्थियों की पिछली लहरों में शामिल हो गए जो उत्पीड़न से बच गए थे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Persecution' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Persecution' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — लगभग 1.2 मिलियन रोहिंग्या अब बांग्लादेश के कॉक्स बाज़ार में भीड़भाड़ वाले शिविरों में रहते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — भारत, मलेशिया और इंडोनेशिया जैसे अन्य देशों में रोहिंग्या शरणार्थियों को अनिश्चित कानूनी स्थिति, भेदभाव, हिरासत और निर्वासन के खतरे का भी सामना करना पड़ता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Discrimination' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Discrimination' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — इस बीच, उनकी मातृभूमि बेहद परेशान बनी हुई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — राखीन राज्य म्यांमार की सेना और अराकान सेना, एक विद्रोही समूह, के बीच लड़ाई में घिरा हुआ है, जो अब इस क्षेत्र के अधिकांश हिस्से को नियंत्रित करता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — रोहिंग्या, जिनमें से कई आंतरिक रूप से विस्थापित हैं, नए सिरे से असुरक्षा, मानवीय पहुंच पर प्रतिबंध और प्रतिस्पर्धी सशस्त्र बलों से हिंसा के खतरे का सामना कर रहे हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — और शरणार्थियों के लिए, अपनी मातृभूमि में वापसी न तो वांछनीय है और न ही व्यावहारिक है।।

hinglishTracks.en: While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — हालांकि आईसीजे का फैसला महत्वपूर्ण है और एक मजबूत मिसाल कायम करता है, लेकिन इससे रोहिंग्या की पीड़ा कम होने की संभावना नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — सुरक्षित बंदरगाह की तलाश: 8 अप्रैल, 2013 को शरणार्थियों को लकड़ी की नाव से क्रुएंग राया, आचे बेसर, इंडोनेशिया में एक अस्थायी आश्रय में ले जाया जा रहा था।।

hinglishTracks.en: The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — यह बंदरगाह वर्षों से एक प्रमुख लैंडिंग बिंदु और अस्थायी आश्रय स्थल रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — नरक से भागना: रोहिंग्या शरणार्थी 2017 में बांग्लादेश के पास म्यांमार में कथित तौर पर सेना द्वारा शुरू की गई आग की पृष्ठभूमि में भाग गए।।

hinglishTracks.en: Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — निर्वासन में नौकायन: रोहिंग्या शरणार्थी 12 नवंबर, 2017 को बांग्लादेश पहुंचने के लिए एक तात्कालिक नाव पर नफ़ नदी पार करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Longing for justice: Rohingya refugees watch the live announcement of the verdict in a genocide case against Myanmar on November 19, 2026
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — न्याय की चाह: रोहिंग्या शरणार्थी 19 नवंबर, 2026 को म्यांमार के खिलाफ नरसंहार मामले में फैसले की लाइव घोषणा देखते हैं। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Announcement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Announcement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The agony of loss: Hamida, a Rohingya refugee, weeps as she holds her 40-day-old son, who died after their boat capsized before reaching the shore in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on September 14, 2017.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — नुकसान की पीड़ा: रोहिंग्या शरणार्थी हमीदा अपने 40 दिन के बेटे को गोद में लेकर रोती है, जिसकी 14 सितंबर, 2017 को बांग्लादेश के टेकनाफ में तट पर पहुंचने से पहले नाव पलटने से मौत हो गई थी।।

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displacement

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:13:36 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: T he International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s top court, on November 19, ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the military’s 2017 clearance operations in Rakhine State. This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide. The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods. In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution. Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation. Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled. Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region. The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces. And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical. While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya. Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013. The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years. Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017. Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017. Longing for justice: Rohingya refugees watch the live announcement of the verdict in a genocide case against Myanmar on November 19, 2026

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agony of loss: Hamida, a Rohingya refugee, weeps as she holds her 40-day-old son, who died after their boat capsized before reaching the shore in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on September 14, 2017.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

Announcement (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Announcement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Persecution (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Persecution' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displacement", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'News in Frames | Living with the wounds of di' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'News in Frames | Living with the wounds of di' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and..." (Hinglish Arth: आईसीजे का फैसला कि म्यांमार ने रोहिंग्या के खिलाफ नरसंहार किया है, महत्वपूर्ण है, लेकिन शरणार्थियों को हिंसा के खतरे और मानवीय पहुंच पर प्रतिबंध का सामना करना पड़ रहा है, क्योंकि उनकी मातृभूमि में स्थिति अभी भी बनी हुई है।)

• 1. Core Context & Background: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: T he International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s top court, on November 19, ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the military’s 2017 clearance operations in Rakhine State. This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide. The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods. In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution. Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation. Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled. Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region. The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces. And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical. While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya. Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013. The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years. Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017. Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia. The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya. The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years. The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”. Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:31:02 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia. The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya. The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years. The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”. Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Rohingya crisis / The Hindu Profiles / Myanmar / United Nations

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Compensation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: Delhi records ‘poor’ AQI, minimum temperature settles at 11.8°C
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: IGNOU-Maidan Garhi recorded the highest AQI at 377, followed by Uttam Nagar at 340

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index of 237 — in the ‘poor’ category — at 9 a.m., official data showed. Of the 54 monitoring stations, 36 recorded ‘poor’ AQI, while five were in the ‘very poor’ category, according to the Sameer app developed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). IGNOU-Maidan Garhi recorded the highest AQI at 377, followed by Uttam Nagar at 340. On the weather front, Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 11.8°C on Sunday (November 22, 2026), slightly down from 12.2 degrees recorded on Saturday (November 21), and about the same as the season's average, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The weather office has forecast clear skies, with maximum temperature expected to touch 27°C. The relative humidity was recorded at 96% at 8:30 a.m. The CPCB classifies an AQI between zero and 50 as 'good', 51 and 100 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 'moderate', 201 and 300 'poor', 301 and 400 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Delhi's AQI remained ‘poor’ on Saturday (November 21), settling at 265 and showing gradual improvement over the last three days. The AQI fell from 280 on November 19 to 270 on November 20 and further to 265 on Saturday (November 21).

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Delhi records ‘poor’ AQI, minimum temperature settles at 11.8°C

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:45:52 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: IGNOU-Maidan Garhi recorded the highest AQI at 377, followed by Uttam Nagar at 340

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index of 237 — in the ‘poor’ category — at 9 a.m., official data showed. Of the 54 monitoring stations, 36 recorded ‘poor’ AQI, while five were in the ‘very poor’ category, according to the Sameer app developed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). IGNOU-Maidan Garhi recorded the highest AQI at 377, followed by Uttam Nagar at 340. On the weather front, Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 11.8°C on Sunday (November 22, 2026), slightly down from 12.2 degrees recorded on Saturday (November 21), and about the same as the season's average, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The weather office has forecast clear skies, with maximum temperature expected to touch 27°C. The relative humidity was recorded at 96% at 8:30 a.m. The CPCB classifies an AQI between zero and 50 as 'good', 51 and 100 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 'moderate', 201 and 300 'poor', 301 and 400 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Delhi's AQI remained ‘poor’ on Saturday (November 21), settling at 265 and showing gradual improvement over the last three days. The AQI fell from 280 on November 19 to 270 on November 20 and further to 265 on Saturday (November 21).

articles.title: BJP leader demands halt to water supply to industries amid scarcity in Latur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped immediately

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: BJP leader Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar has demanded the immediate rollout of the ₹24,000-crore Marathwada Water Grid project and a halt on supply to industries from the depleting Manjara dam to tackle the growing scarcity in Latur. Expressing concern over dwindling water levels, Mr. Kavhekar on Saturday (November 22) said the Manjara dam has only 4% live storage, yet water continues to be supplied to sugar factories and industries. He demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped immediately. The former MLA was speaking after a delegation of the Jan Nayak Sanghatana led by him submitted a memorandum of demands to Additional Collector Shilpa Karmarkar and Resident Deputy Collector Keshav Netke, highlighting pressing water and agrarian issues in Latur district and the Marathwada region. "Not a single drop of water has reached Latur from the Ujani water supply scheme even 22 years after its inauguration," he said, adding that while a ₹135-crore internal water supply scheme was previously executed in Latur city and work on a second pipeline is underway, the municipal corporation has submitted a fresh proposal for another scheme to the state government. Mr. Kavhekar said the proposed Marathwada Water Grid, designed to interconnect major reservoirs including Jayakwadi and Manjara, is vital to resolving the region's long-term water shortage. Raising issues concerning farmers, he demanded crop loss compensation of ₹50,000 per hectare for up to three hectares, over and above the ₹5,000 assistance already announced by the government, along with the immediate disbursement of pending crop insurance claims for 2024-25 and 2025-26.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also sought a waiver of farm and allied-sector loans, including poultry farming, from nationalised, urban cooperative and district central cooperative banks.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 BJP leader demands halt to water supply to industries amid scarcity in Latur

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:33:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped immediately

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: BJP leader Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar has demanded the immediate rollout of the ₹24,000-crore Marathwada Water Grid project and a halt on supply to industries from the depleting Manjara dam to tackle the growing scarcity in Latur. Expressing concern over dwindling water levels, Mr. Kavhekar on Saturday (November 22) said the Manjara dam has only 4% live storage, yet water continues to be supplied to sugar factories and industries. He demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped immediately. The former MLA was speaking after a delegation of the Jan Nayak Sanghatana led by him submitted a memorandum of demands to Additional Collector Shilpa Karmarkar and Resident Deputy Collector Keshav Netke, highlighting pressing water and agrarian issues in Latur district and the Marathwada region. "Not a single drop of water has reached Latur from the Ujani water supply scheme even 22 years after its inauguration," he said, adding that while a ₹135-crore internal water supply scheme was previously executed in Latur city and work on a second pipeline is underway, the municipal corporation has submitted a fresh proposal for another scheme to the state government. Mr. Kavhekar said the proposed Marathwada Water Grid, designed to interconnect major reservoirs including Jayakwadi and Manjara, is vital to resolving the region's long-term water shortage. Raising issues concerning farmers, he demanded crop loss compensation of ₹50,000 per hectare for up to three hectares, over and above the ₹5,000 assistance already announced by the government, along with the immediate disbursement of pending crop insurance claims for 2024-25 and 2025-26.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also sought a waiver of farm and allied-sector loans, including poultry farming, from nationalised, urban cooperative and district central cooperative banks.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Inauguration (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Inauguration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Compensation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Compensation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Disbursement (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Disbursement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Corporation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Corporation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "BJP leader demands halt to water supply to industries amid scarcity in Latur", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'BJP leader demands halt to water supply to indus' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'BJP leader demands halt to water supply to in' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'BJP leader demands halt to water supply to in' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Shivajirao Patil Kavhekar demanded that drinking water needs of rural and urban areas be given top priority and industrial supply be stopped..." (Hinglish Arth: शिवाजीराव पाटिल कव्हेकर ने मांग की कि ग्रामीण और शहरी क्षेत्रों की पेयजल जरूरतों को सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता दी जाए और औद्योगिक आपूर्ति तुरंत बंद की जाए)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "BJP leader demands halt to water supply to industries amid scarcity in Latur"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He also sought a waiver of farm and allied-sector loans, including poultry farming, from nationalised, urban cooperative and district central...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "He also sought a waiver of farm and allied-sector loans, including poultry farming, from nationalised, urban cooperative and district central..." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने राष्ट्रीयकृत, शहरी सहकारी और जिला केंद्रीय सहकारी बैंकों से मुर्गी पालन सहित कृषि और संबद्ध क्षेत्र के ऋणों की माफी की भी मांग की।)

articles.title: Pranab Doley | Confronting the State
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The rights activist in Assam is asking why indigenous people are being criminalised while defending their land and heritage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pranab Doley, 40, describes himself as a first-generation learner. He graduated in Arts from Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan in 2009 and earned a Master’s in Social Welfare from Mumbai ’s Tata Institute of Social Sciences two years later. Rather than pursue a conventional career, he turned to grassroots organising, helping found and lead bodies such as Jeepal Krishak Shramik Sangha (JKSS), a farmers’ rights group, and the All Kaziranga Affected Communities’ Rights Committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: His fight for indigenous land rights in Assam has repeatedly brought him into confrontation with the State government, the latest ending in a 118-day detention under the National Security Act (NSA) for opposing a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park. For Mr. Doley, it was another chapter in a long history of arrests connected to his activism.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Pranab Doley | Confronting the State

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:21:43 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The rights activist in Assam is asking why indigenous people are being criminalised while defending their land and heritage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pranab Doley, 40, describes himself as a first-generation learner. He graduated in Arts from Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan in 2009 and earned a Master’s in Social Welfare from Mumbai ’s Tata Institute of Social Sciences two years later. Rather than pursue a conventional career, he turned to grassroots organising, helping found and lead bodies such as Jeepal Krishak Shramik Sangha (JKSS), a farmers’ rights group, and the All Kaziranga Affected Communities’ Rights Committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: His fight for indigenous land rights in Assam has repeatedly brought him into confrontation with the State government, the latest ending in a 118-day detention under the National Security Act (NSA) for opposing a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park. For Mr. Doley, it was another chapter in a long history of arrests connected to his activism.

Indigenous (Adjective)

Confrontation (Noun)

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conventional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Pranab Doley | Confronting the State' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status. According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status. The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030. The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment. According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres. The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment. Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October. The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets. Mr. Satya Kumar said priority was to ensure timely diagnosis, continuous treatment and quality healthcare without discrimination for everyone living with HIV.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: APSACS Project Director Smaran Raj said the organisation was committed to bringing three more districts to ‘Surakshit’ status in the week.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:15:23 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status. According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status. The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030. The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment. According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres. The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment. Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October. The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets. Mr. Satya Kumar said priority was to ensure timely diagnosis, continuous treatment and quality healthcare without discrimination for everyone living with HIV.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: APSACS Project Director Smaran Raj said the organisation was committed to bringing three more districts to ‘Surakshit’ status in the week.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Discrimination' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Organisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Organisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Performance (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Performance' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

A. Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s...

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer ‘test’ website, wanted to earn money by selling it on dark web: Delhi police sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu . The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces. “Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said. During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money. “He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined. After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database. The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach. The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised. While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action.
