🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:47:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures. That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says. Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area. Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals. From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / food / food / food and dining (general) / food security / traditional food / India / India / arable farming / Agriculture / agriculture

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'One country, hundreds of dal recipes: explori' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'One country, hundreds of dal recipes: explori' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures. That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says. Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area. Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals. From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / food / food / food and dining (general) / food security / traditional food / India / India / arable farming / Agriculture / agriculture

articles.title: CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ‘anti-drone gun’ on IndiaMART
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The CCPA held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 lakh on AirOne Robotics Pvt Ltd for listing and advertising an "Anti-drone gun VKSP03-PRO" on e-commerce platform IndiaMART without mandatory disclosures and regulatory authorisations. In its recent order, CCPA chief commissioner Nidhi Khare and commissioner Anupam Mishra held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices. The authority observed that "maintaining an active commercial listing with full technical specifications, an ₹8,30,000 price point and an 'In stock' indicator on a prominent marketplace e-commerce entity clearly established an intent to offer the goods for sale and solicit prospective buyers." The company had claimed the product was a "non-active/inert replica". Rejecting this, CCPA said it was "a bare assertion, made only after the Show Cause Notice and contradicted by the listing itself", and could not be accepted as proof. It also noted that the firm's own versions were not "consistent with one another". CCPA also turned down the firm's contention that terms like "Anti-drone gun", "electronic warfare device" and "neutralising drones" were used "purely as descriptive titles" to convey the "aesthetic design" of the model, and that the listing was "purely conceptual and ornamental". The regulator said whether actual sales took place, or whether the product was later claimed to be an inert dummy, does not lessen the advertiser's culpability. Hosting and advertising restricted electronic warfare equipment without statutory authorisations and mandatory civilian prohibition disclosures under the Cabinet Secretariat's jammer guidelines and telecom laws amounts to a deceptive advertisement and unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, it held. The company has been directed to ensure all future advertisements and listings comply with the Act and do not carry any false or misleading claims on the operational capabilities, availability or lawful use of such equipment. It must submit a compliance report within 15 days of the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incorporated in March 2026, AirOne Robotics has its registered office in Howrah, West Bengal. It is engaged in manufacturing and wholesale trade of machinery and equipment, engineering and technical consultancy, and manufacture of radar equipment, GPS devices, and search, detection and navigation equipment.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ‘anti-drone gun’ on IndiaMART

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 03:25:53 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The CCPA held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 lakh on AirOne Robotics Pvt Ltd for listing and advertising an "Anti-drone gun VKSP03-PRO" on e-commerce platform IndiaMART without mandatory disclosures and regulatory authorisations. In its recent order, CCPA chief commissioner Nidhi Khare and commissioner Anupam Mishra held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices. The authority observed that "maintaining an active commercial listing with full technical specifications, an ₹8,30,000 price point and an 'In stock' indicator on a prominent marketplace e-commerce entity clearly established an intent to offer the goods for sale and solicit prospective buyers." The company had claimed the product was a "non-active/inert replica". Rejecting this, CCPA said it was "a bare assertion, made only after the Show Cause Notice and contradicted by the listing itself", and could not be accepted as proof. It also noted that the firm's own versions were not "consistent with one another". CCPA also turned down the firm's contention that terms like "Anti-drone gun", "electronic warfare device" and "neutralising drones" were used "purely as descriptive titles" to convey the "aesthetic design" of the model, and that the listing was "purely conceptual and ornamental". The regulator said whether actual sales took place, or whether the product was later claimed to be an inert dummy, does not lessen the advertiser's culpability. Hosting and advertising restricted electronic warfare equipment without statutory authorisations and mandatory civilian prohibition disclosures under the Cabinet Secretariat's jammer guidelines and telecom laws amounts to a deceptive advertisement and unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, it held. The company has been directed to ensure all future advertisements and listings comply with the Act and do not carry any false or misleading claims on the operational capabilities, availability or lawful use of such equipment. It must submit a compliance report within 15 days of the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Incorporated in March 2026, AirOne Robotics has its registered office in Howrah, West Bengal. It is engaged in manufacturing and wholesale trade of machinery and equipment, engineering and technical consultancy, and manufacture of radar equipment, GPS devices, and search, detection and navigation equipment.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Prospective' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ‘anti-drone gun’ on IndiaMART", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The CCPA held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ‘an' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The CCPA held the company guilty of violating consumer rights, issuing misleading advertisements and indulging in unfair trade practices." (Hinglish Arth: सीसीपीए ने कंपनी को उपभोक्ता अधिकारों का उल्लंघन करने, भ्रामक विज्ञापन जारी करने और अनुचित व्यापार प्रथाओं में शामिल होने का दोषी ठहराया)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on firm for selling ‘anti-drone gun’ on IndiaMART"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. It is engaged in manufacturing and wholesale trade of machinery and equipment, engineering and technical consultancy, and manufacture of radar...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "It is engaged in manufacturing and wholesale trade of machinery and equipment, engineering and technical consultancy, and manufacture of radar..." (Hinglish Arth: यह मशीनरी और उपकरणों के विनिर्माण और थोक व्यापार, इंजीनियरिंग और तकनीकी परामर्श, और रडार उपकरण, जीपीएस उपकरणों और खोज, पहचान और नेविगेशन उपकरणों के निर्माण में लगा हुआ है।)

articles.title: Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls for balance between tribal rights, development
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kiren Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to investment and development.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said Arunachal Pradesh must find ways to become economically self-reliant and called for a broader debate on how the state can attract investment, technology and modern facilities while safeguarding the identity of its people, land rights and cultural heritage. Addressing a function, the Parliamentary and Minority Affairs Minister said Arunachal Pradesh was a special state from the constitutional perspective and faced several challenges because of its "tribal character, limited resources and restrictions on land ownership". Mr. Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to investment and development. While people rightly emphasised the protection of human and land rights, tribal identity and cultural traditions, the developmental challenges arising from constitutional provisions also needed equal attention, he said. Mr. Rijiju pointed out that Arunachal Pradesh has limited capital and technological resources and will have to depend on outside investment and expertise to meet its development needs. However, restrictions on land ownership often posed challenges to attracting industrialists and investors, he said. The minister said the state should explore ways to "become self-reliant by effectively utilising its available resources, particularly in agriculture, horticulture and tourism. These sectors have considerable potential to strengthen the local economy and create livelihood opportunities". Mr. Rijiju said Arunachal Pradesh had made rapid progress since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He said visits by Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah to the State had brought fresh momentum to development activities and generated renewed enthusiasm among the people. Their leadership and support had helped Arunachal Pradesh move forward, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to his position in the Union Cabinet, Mr. Rijiju said he felt proud to be part of the government and to witness the support being extended to the state's development.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls for balance between tribal rights, development

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 03:25:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kiren Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to investment and development.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said Arunachal Pradesh must find ways to become economically self-reliant and called for a broader debate on how the state can attract investment, technology and modern facilities while safeguarding the identity of its people, land rights and cultural heritage. Addressing a function, the Parliamentary and Minority Affairs Minister said Arunachal Pradesh was a special state from the constitutional perspective and faced several challenges because of its "tribal character, limited resources and restrictions on land ownership". Mr. Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to investment and development. While people rightly emphasised the protection of human and land rights, tribal identity and cultural traditions, the developmental challenges arising from constitutional provisions also needed equal attention, he said. Mr. Rijiju pointed out that Arunachal Pradesh has limited capital and technological resources and will have to depend on outside investment and expertise to meet its development needs. However, restrictions on land ownership often posed challenges to attracting industrialists and investors, he said. The minister said the state should explore ways to "become self-reliant by effectively utilising its available resources, particularly in agriculture, horticulture and tourism. These sectors have considerable potential to strengthen the local economy and create livelihood opportunities". Mr. Rijiju said Arunachal Pradesh had made rapid progress since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He said visits by Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah to the State had brought fresh momentum to development activities and generated renewed enthusiasm among the people. Their leadership and support had helped Arunachal Pradesh move forward, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to his position in the Union Cabinet, Mr. Rijiju said he felt proud to be part of the government and to witness the support being extended to the state's development.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Developmental (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Developmental' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls for balance between tribal rights, development", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kiren Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls fo' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Kiren Rijiju stressed the need to find a balance between protecting the interests of indigenous communities and creating an environment conducive to..." (Hinglish Arth: किरेन रिजिजू ने स्वदेशी समुदायों के हितों की रक्षा और निवेश और विकास के लिए अनुकूल माहौल बनाने के बीच संतुलन खोजने की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Rijiju bats for self-reliant Arunachal, calls for balance between tribal rights, development"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Rijiju said he felt proud to be part of the government and to witness the support being extended to the state's development.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Rijiju said he felt proud to be part of the government and to witness the support being extended to the state's development." articles.title: Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review plea in Supreme Court against Thirupparankundram order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial precedents or violated a statutory mandate

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Forty-eight hours before the lighting of the lamp at the deepathoon on Karthigai Deepam day on November 24, the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department filed a review of the Supreme Court’s interim order allowing the “one-time limited arrangement”. The review jurisdiction is a rare remedy, and not to be used as an appeal in disguise or as an opportunity to re-argue the case on merits. The parties seeking a review of an apex court decision must prove the decision was erroneous on the face of the record. The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial precedents or violated a statutory mandate. The review petition is placed before the same Bench which passed the decision under question. It is usually examined in chambers by circulation. On November 20, a Division Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a restricted and one-off measure, on the deepathoon at the Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24, 2026). The Supreme Court repeatedly made it plain that this interim order allowing the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon would not give any vested, enforceable right or entitlement to anyone. It had underscored that the interim and singular arrangement for November 24, 2026 should not be shown as a precedent for claiming similar permission in any subsequent year. “Neither the permission granted by this court nor the performance of the ceremony pursuant thereto shall be relied upon by any party as evidence of an established custom, precedent of religious usage, possessory right, entitlement to access or alteration of the existing legal position till adjudication of these appeals,” the court had clarified. Justice Kumar had clarified that the larger issues of religious rights and tradition raised by the State in its appeal against a January 2026 judgment of a Division Bench of the Madras High Court, which had confirmed an earlier Single Judge direction to the Arulmigu Subramaniswamy Temple devasthanam to light the Karthigai Deepam on the stone pillar located at the summit of the Thirupparankundram Hill near a dargah, would be subject to detailed judicial review. 📰 Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review plea in Supreme Court against Thirupparankundram order

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 03:20:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial precedents or violated a statutory mandate

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Forty-eight hours before the lighting of the lamp at the deepathoon on Karthigai Deepam day on November 24, the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department filed a review of the Supreme Court’s interim order allowing the “one-time limited arrangement”. The review jurisdiction is a rare remedy, and not to be used as an appeal in disguise or as an opportunity to re-argue the case on merits. The parties seeking a review of an apex court decision must prove the decision was erroneous on the face of the record. The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial precedents or violated a statutory mandate. The review petition is placed before the same Bench which passed the decision under question. It is usually examined in chambers by circulation. On November 20, a Division Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a restricted and one-off measure, on the deepathoon at the Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24, 2026). The Supreme Court repeatedly made it plain that this interim order allowing the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon would not give any vested, enforceable right or entitlement to anyone. It had underscored that the interim and singular arrangement for November 24, 2026 should not be shown as a precedent for claiming similar permission in any subsequent year. “Neither the permission granted by this court nor the performance of the ceremony pursuant thereto shall be relied upon by any party as evidence of an established custom, precedent of religious usage, possessory right, entitlement to access or alteration of the existing legal position till adjudication of these appeals,” the court had clarified. Justice Kumar had clarified that the larger issues of religious rights and tradition raised by the State in its appeal against a January 2026 judgment of a Division Bench of the Madras High Court, which had confirmed an earlier Single Judge direction to the Arulmigu Subramaniswamy Temple devasthanam to light the Karthigai Deepam on the stone pillar located at the summit of the Thirupparankundram Hill near a dargah, would be subject to detailed judicial review. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thirupparankundram row: T.N. govt pushes for stay of HC order to avoid breach of peace

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Permissibility (Noun)
कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।
✓ Syn: Admissibility, Legality, Allowance  |  ✖ Ant: Prohibition, Ban, Illegality
Jurisdiction (Noun)
अधिकार क्षेत्र — न्यायालय या किसी संस्था की वह कानूनी सीमा जहाँ तक वह आदेश दे सके।
✓ Syn: Authority, Sovereignty, Cognizance  |  ✖ Ant: Powerlessness, Subordination, Incompetence
Misconception (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Misconception' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review plea i' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review ple' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review ple' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The party urging a re-look of the court order must show that the findings were a result of a factual misconception or had ignored binding judicial..." (Hinglish Arth: अदालत के आदेश पर दोबारा विचार करने का आग्रह करने वाली पार्टी को यह दिखाना होगा कि निष्कर्ष तथ्यात्मक ग़लतफ़हमी का परिणाम थे या उन्होंने बाध्यकारी न्यायिक मिसालों की अनदेखी की थी या वैधानिक आदेश का उल्लंघन किया था।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review plea in Supreme Court against Thirupparankundram order"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. govt pushes for stay of HC order to avoid breach of peace.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "govt pushes for stay of HC order to avoid breach of peace." (Hinglish Arth: शांति भंग होने से बचने के लिए सरकार उच्च न्यायालय के आदेश पर रोक लगाने पर जोर दे रही है)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prices of prominent metals including gold, copper and aluminium tumbled to at least seven-month lows on hawkish commentary about U.S. Fed seeking to increase rates and weighing concerns over global economic growth in the immediate term. Benchmark price of the yellow metal, that is, at the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) slipped to their lowest since September 2025 to close this week at $3,521.38 per troy ounce. Further, benchmark price of copper — that is, at the London Metal Exchange (LME) — slipped to their lowest in about eight months at $12,230.40 per metric tonne. Reference price for aluminium at LME also slipped to an almost one-year low at $2,824.5 per metric tonne. Gold prices in 2026 have taken a nosedive from where they began the year, with the yellow metal falling over 25% from its peak, with a majority of the unwinding taking place over the last couple of months. Gold has seen exponential growth since 2022, rising 145% globally till now, with prices hitting multiple record highs last year. Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Limited, says the primary driver of the downswing in gold prices is the change in global macroeconomic conditions. “The biggest driver (in price movements) is that the macro story changed. Since the (Iran-U.S.) war, inflation expectations, energy prices, and anticipation of interest rate hikes capped gains for the metal.” With traders expecting a more hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, the U.S. dollar has also gained strength in recent weeks. It is important to note that gold typically thrives in a weak-dollar environment. U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s remarks last week further cemented expectations of a rate hike next month.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the target range to 4.00–4.25%.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 03:19:41 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Hawkish commentary from U.S. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prices of prominent metals including gold, copper and aluminium tumbled to at least seven-month lows on hawkish commentary about U.S. Fed seeking to increase rates and weighing concerns over global economic growth in the immediate term. Benchmark price of the yellow metal, that is, at the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) slipped to their lowest since September 2025 to close this week at $3,521.38 per troy ounce. Further, benchmark price of copper — that is, at the London Metal Exchange (LME) — slipped to their lowest in about eight months at $12,230.40 per metric tonne. Reference price for aluminium at LME also slipped to an almost one-year low at $2,824.5 per metric tonne. Gold prices in 2026 have taken a nosedive from where they began the year, with the yellow metal falling over 25% from its peak, with a majority of the unwinding taking place over the last couple of months. Gold has seen exponential growth since 2022, rising 145% globally till now, with prices hitting multiple record highs last year. Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Limited, says the primary driver of the downswing in gold prices is the change in global macroeconomic conditions. “The biggest driver (in price movements) is that the macro story changed. Since the (Iran-U.S.) war, inflation expectations, energy prices, and anticipation of interest rate hikes capped gains for the metal.” With traders expecting a more hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, the U.S. dollar has also gained strength in recent weeks. It is important to note that gold typically thrives in a weak-dollar environment. U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s remarks last week further cemented expectations of a rate hike next month.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the target range to 4.00–4.25%.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Macroeconomic (Adjective)
समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र — पूरे देश की अर्थव्यवस्था (GDP, महंगाई, RBI नीति, रोज़गार) से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Fiscal-scale, National-economic, Aggregate  |  ✖ Ant: Microeconomic, Individual, Local
Inflation (Noun)
महंगाई (मुद्रास्फीति) — जब बाज़ार में वस्तुओं के दाम बढ़ें और रुपये की खरीद शक्ति कम हो जाए।
✓ Syn: Price-escalation, Hyperinflation, Dearness  |  ✖ Ant: Deflation, Disinflation, Recession
Anticipation (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Anticipation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Fed and concerns over global economic growth have been among the more prominent concerns.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-mo' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-mo' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Gold, copper, aluminium dive to at least 7-month lows"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 95% probability of the Fed hiking interest rates by a quarter percentage point next month, taking the...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A juvenile court ordered that six persons in the 12- to 15-year-old age group be placed in a juvenile home until December 4, after Ghatkopar police detained eight persons below 18 in connection with an assault on a couple at Pramod Mahajan Garden in Kurla on Friday evening (November 20, 2026) and produced all eight before the Juvenile Justice Board, police said. Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an officer said. According to police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of persons in the 12-15 age group surrounded them and began to abuse them; when the couple tried to reason with the group, the persons assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden, and police detained the eight after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. Police said they were recording statements from the couple and the persons below 18 to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident, and an officer said, “We are finding out what was the reason for the assault.” Samajwadi Party’s Maharashtra unit president Abu Asim Azmi said the age for juveniles should be brought down from 18 to 15 and said persons below 18 who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not receive concessions under the law; he said the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination. Nitesh Rane, a BJP leader, commented on the video, saying, “This isn’t their father’s Pakistan,” and added that he “would send a person who wore a skullcap and had a beard to Aurangzeb if an incident happened again.” BJP leader Kirit Somaiya, who was an MP, visited the garden on Saturday (November 21), met the couple at Ghatkopar police station, sought action, and said he would raise concerns about security with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the home portfolio, to adopt a policy of no tolerance when incidents occur and said citizens should be able to move around freely; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui condemned the assault and said police were doing their job.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mumbai / law / crime / police / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / Shiv Sena

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 03:06:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A juvenile court ordered that six persons in the 12- to 15-year-old age group be placed in a juvenile home until December 4, after Ghatkopar police detained eight persons below 18 in connection with an assault on a couple at Pramod Mahajan Garden in Kurla on Friday evening (November 20, 2026) and produced all eight before the Juvenile Justice Board, police said. Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an officer said. According to police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of persons in the 12-15 age group surrounded them and began to abuse them; when the couple tried to reason with the group, the persons assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden, and police detained the eight after a video of the incident surfaced on social media. Police said they were recording statements from the couple and the persons below 18 to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident, and an officer said, “We are finding out what was the reason for the assault.” Samajwadi Party’s Maharashtra unit president Abu Asim Azmi said the age for juveniles should be brought down from 18 to 15 and said persons below 18 who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not receive concessions under the law; he said the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination. Nitesh Rane, a BJP leader, commented on the video, saying, “This isn’t their father’s Pakistan,” and added that he “would send a person who wore a skullcap and had a beard to Aurangzeb if an incident happened again.” BJP leader Kirit Somaiya, who was an MP, visited the garden on Saturday (November 21), met the couple at Ghatkopar police station, sought action, and said he would raise concerns about security with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the home portfolio, to adopt a policy of no tolerance when incidents occur and said citizens should be able to move around freely; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui condemned the assault and said police were doing their job.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mumbai / law / crime / police / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / Shiv Sena

Marketcity (Noun)
मार्केटसिटी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Marketcity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2),...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assaul' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assaul' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2),..." (Hinglish Arth: पुलिस ने मामला दर्ज किया और सभी आठों को बोर्ड के सामने पेश किया, और माता-पिता को नोटिस भेजे गए; मामला भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 और 351(2) के तहत दर्ज किया गया था।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Mumbai / law / crime / police / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / Shiv Sena.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Mumbai / law / crime / police / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / Shiv Sena." (Hinglish Arth: मुंबई/कानून/अपराध/पुलिस/समाजवादी पार्टी/भारतीय जनता पार्टी/शिवसेना)

articles.title: i-ALERT system leads to savings, lesser emissions for RTC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) announced that they are the first State Road Transport Corporation in India to introduce the i-ALERT system in its BS-VI buses and indicated its implementation has saved the organisation approximately ₹36 crore in diesel costs. According to the state-run road transport undertaking, the i-ALERT tool monitors and assesses driving patterns. It keeps tabs on gear selection, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and braking practices, thus assisting drivers to adopt safer and more fuel-efficient driving methods. The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month. The corporation estimates its monthly savings at ₹2 crore. The reduction in fuel consumption has also cut carbon emissions. With every litre of diesel estimated to generate 2.56 kg of carbon emissions, the initiative has helped reduce CO2 emissions by 16.90 metric tonnes a day, 507.11 tonnes a month and 6,169.84 tons annually, the TGSRTC stated. The system also enables the corporation to assess individual driver performance after every duty and provide feedback and grades. Drivers are monitored for adherence to the prescribed Green Band RPM range, efficient use of economy gears, reduction in engine idling, avoidance of over speeding and appropriate braking practices. TGSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Anil Kumar congratulated the engineering department for adopting the technology. He urged other departments to adopt modern technology to further improve the corporation’s services.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: APSRTC and KSRTC have approached senior TGSRTC officials seeking information on the performance of the i-ALERT system, the corporation said.

According to the state-run road transport undertaking, the i-ALERT tool monitors and assesses driving patterns. It keeps tabs on gear selection, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and braking practices, thus assisting drivers to adopt safer and more fuel-efficient driving methods. The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month. The corporation estimates its monthly savings at ₹2 crore. The reduction in fuel consumption has also cut carbon emissions. With every litre of diesel estimated to generate 2.56 kg of carbon emissions, the initiative has helped reduce CO2 emissions by 16.90 metric tonnes a day, 507.11 tonnes a month and 6,169.84 tons annually, the TGSRTC stated. The system also enables the corporation to assess individual driver performance after every duty and provide feedback and grades. Drivers are monitored for adherence to the prescribed Green Band RPM range, efficient use of economy gears, reduction in engine idling, avoidance of over speeding and appropriate braking practices. TGSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Anil Kumar congratulated the engineering department for adopting the technology. He urged other departments to adopt modern technology to further improve the corporation’s services.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) announced that they are the first State Road Transport Corporation in India to introduce the i-ALERT system in its BS-VI buses and indicated its implementation has saved the organisation approximately ₹36 crore in diesel costs. According to the state-run road transport undertaking, the i-ALERT tool monitors and assesses driving patterns. It keeps tabs on gear selection, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and braking practices, thus assisting drivers to adopt safer and more fuel-efficient driving methods. The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month. The corporation estimates its monthly savings at ₹2 crore. The reduction in fuel consumption has also cut carbon emissions. With every litre of diesel estimated to generate 2.56 kg of carbon emissions, the initiative has helped reduce CO2 emissions by 16.90 metric tonnes a day, 507.11 tonnes a month and 6,169.84 tons annually, the TGSRTC stated. The system also enables the corporation to assess individual driver performance after every duty and provide feedback and grades. Drivers are monitored for adherence to the prescribed Green Band RPM range, efficient use of economy gears, reduction in engine idling, avoidance of over speeding and appropriate braking practices. TGSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Anil Kumar congratulated the engineering department for adopting the technology. He urged other departments to adopt modern technology to further improve the corporation’s services.

articles.title: Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: We were weak, but we are not weak now. We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party, says Rajendra Pal Gautam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Congress is hopeful of forging an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election but wants a “respectable” seat-sharing arrangement, All India Congress Committee in-charge for the State Rajendra Pal Gautam has said. Mr. Gautam, in an interview with The Hindu , said the two parties are expected to hold formal seat-sharing discussions this week and asserted that the Congress would make the alleged “ chanda chori ” (theft of temple donations) a major campaign issue. Though he did not disclose the exact date, the first meeting is likely to be held on Monday afternoon. Senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K.C. Venugopal, and Mr. Gautam, are expected to participate. Commenting on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s recent statement that the Congress had sought 181 seats, Mr. Gautam said, “I am not going to reveal which seats, but we have given them a list. We will try to convince them, and I am sure they will try to convince us. The outcome depends on these talks.” Asked whether the Congress would settle for an alliance at any cost, Mr. Gautam said: “It is not like that at all. The understanding will be a respectable one.” Countering suggestions that the Congress lacked the organisational strength to bargain for a substantial share of seats, Mr. Gautam pointed out that while the SP won 37 seats and the Congress six in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP’s alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls had not yielded similar results. “We were weak, but we are not weak now,” he said, adding, “We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party.” On whether the Congress was attempting social engineering to regain the support of the Brahmin, Dalit, and Muslim communities that had once formed its core constituency, he claimed that every section of society is now gravitating toward the party. “Every section is feeling cheated, whether Brahmins, Dalits, OBCs, or Muslims,” he said. The party also intends to highlight the alleged chadhava-chori (theft of offerings and donations) at Lord Ram’s temple in Ayodhya. The campaign, scheduled to begin in the first week of December, will take the issue to villages, chaupals, and gram panchayats.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “ Chadhava-chori, chanda-chori will be one of our main issues in the election. The BJP came to power using faith and then betrayed the people. In every press conference and public meeting, we will raise it,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 05:21:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: We were weak, but we are not weak now. We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party, says Rajendra Pal Gautam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Congress is hopeful of forging an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election but wants a “respectable” seat-sharing arrangement, All India Congress Committee in-charge for the State Rajendra Pal Gautam has said. Mr. Gautam, in an interview with The Hindu , said the two parties are expected to hold formal seat-sharing discussions this week and asserted that the Congress would make the alleged “ chanda chori ” (theft of temple donations) a major campaign issue. Though he did not disclose the exact date, the first meeting is likely to be held on Monday afternoon. Senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K.C. Venugopal, and Mr. Gautam, are expected to participate. Commenting on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s recent statement that the Congress had sought 181 seats, Mr. Gautam said, “I am not going to reveal which seats, but we have given them a list. We will try to convince them, and I am sure they will try to convince us. The outcome depends on these talks.” Asked whether the Congress would settle for an alliance at any cost, Mr. Gautam said: “It is not like that at all. The understanding will be a respectable one.” Countering suggestions that the Congress lacked the organisational strength to bargain for a substantial share of seats, Mr. Gautam pointed out that while the SP won 37 seats and the Congress six in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP’s alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls had not yielded similar results. “We were weak, but we are not weak now,” he said, adding, “We have the best leader in this country right now, as only we can handle the BJP better than any other party.” On whether the Congress was attempting social engineering to regain the support of the Brahmin, Dalit, and Muslim communities that had once formed its core constituency, he claimed that every section of society is now gravitating toward the party. “Every section is feeling cheated, whether Brahmins, Dalits, OBCs, or Muslims,” he said. The party also intends to highlight the alleged chadhava-chori (theft of offerings and donations) at Lord Ram’s temple in Ayodhya. The campaign, scheduled to begin in the first week of December, will take the issue to villages, chaupals, and gram panchayats.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “ Chadhava-chori, chanda-chori will be one of our main issues in the election. The BJP came to power using faith and then betrayed the people. In every press conference and public meeting, we will raise it,” he said.

Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Organisational (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Organisational' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Arrangement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Substantial (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Substantial' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. We were weak, but we are not weak now.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, se' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, se' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "We were weak, but we are not weak now." (Hinglish Arth: हम कमजोर थे, लेकिन अब कमजोर नहीं हैं.')
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Congress hopeful of U.P. alliance with SP, seeks ‘respectable’ seat-sharing"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. In every press conference and public meeting, we will raise it,” he said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "In every press conference and public meeting, we will raise it,” he said." (Hinglish Arth: हम हर प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस और सार्वजनिक बैठक में इसे उठाएंगे।'')

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year. European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year. The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules. Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive. The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU. Watch | India–EU Free Trade Agreement explained: Biggest trade deal in India’s history | India-New Zealand FTA comes into force; new visa categories for Indians, zero-duty access for exports Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion). The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: European Union / India-UK Free Trade Agreement / trade agreements / business (general)

The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules. articles.title: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant teams win three gold awards at international quality convention in Dhaka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: All three Quality Control Circle teams from RINL win the top honour at ICQCC-2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, has secured three Gold Awards at the International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) hosted by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) in Dhaka from November 18 to 20. Participating in the hybrid-mode convention, three Quality Control Circle teams from the steel plant presented their technical case studies online from the Centre for HRD at Ukku House on November 19, with all three entries clinching the top honour. Team ‘AMPS’ from the Blast Furnace department, comprising M.V. Ramana, P. Sai Narendra Kumar, Ahammad Valli, P.M. Satyanarayana and K. Suresh, won the award for their project on modifying the vacuum contactor of the HT motor in the slag granulation plant. From SMS-1, team ‘SAAPHALYA’, represented by G. Siva Sankar Rao, Bhanu Kiran Banda, G. Appa Rao and P. Simhachalam, earned gold for their case study on LD converter ID fan lubrication oil pipeline modification. Team ‘UNNATI’ from the Utilities department, consisting of Niranjan Shailendra, Bhavani Ramyasree Utala, Sugunavathi Seepana and K. Srinivasa Rao, bagged the third gold for devising an innovative method to synchronise a high-pressure 4.5 MW nitrogen compressor motor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The RINL management congratulated the winning teams, noting that the international recognition reflected the workforce’s technical competence, teamwork and commitment to operational excellence.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Visakhapatnam Steel Plant teams win three gold awards at international quality convention in Dhaka

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:50:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: All three Quality Control Circle teams from RINL win the top honour at ICQCC-2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, has secured three Gold Awards at the International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) hosted by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) in Dhaka from November 18 to 20. Participating in the hybrid-mode convention, three Quality Control Circle teams from the steel plant presented their technical case studies online from the Centre for HRD at Ukku House on November 19, with all three entries clinching the top honour. Team ‘AMPS’ from the Blast Furnace department, comprising M.V. Ramana, P. Sai Narendra Kumar, Ahammad Valli, P.M. Satyanarayana and K. Suresh, won the award for their project on modifying the vacuum contactor of the HT motor in the slag granulation plant. From SMS-1, team ‘SAAPHALYA’, represented by G. Siva Sankar Rao, Bhanu Kiran Banda, G. Appa Rao and P. Simhachalam, earned gold for their case study on LD converter ID fan lubrication oil pipeline modification. Team ‘UNNATI’ from the Utilities department, consisting of Niranjan Shailendra, Bhavani Ramyasree Utala, Sugunavathi Seepana and K. Srinivasa Rao, bagged the third gold for devising an innovative method to synchronise a high-pressure 4.5 MW nitrogen compressor motor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The RINL management congratulated the winning teams, noting that the international recognition reflected the workforce’s technical competence, teamwork and commitment to operational excellence.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

दानेदार बनाने का कार्य — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Granulation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:48:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care." (Hinglish Arth: ग्राउंड ज़ीरो/केरलम/शिशु/स्वास्थ्य/सरकारी स्वास्थ्य देखभाल)

articles.title: ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year, claiming gold prices fell due to this. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Mr. Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Mr. Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing, and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM further said, "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji’s request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation."

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:48:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year, claiming gold prices fell due to this. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Mr. Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Mr. Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing, and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM further said, "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji’s request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation."

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Convocation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
