🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: MLA Allamprabhu Patil meets Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar recently and submits a memorandum seeking urgent financial assistance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: MLA Allamprabhu Patil has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to release an additional grant of ₹5 crore to address the worsening drinking water crisis in Kalaburagi city where groundwater levels have reportedly depleted in nearly 80% of the areas, while borewells have gone dry. Mr. Patil met the Chief Minister in Bengaluru recently and submitted a memorandum seeking urgent financial assistance to tackle the situation. In the memorandum, the MLA also drew the Chief Minister’s attention to the extensive crop losses in the district due to drought and sought the early release of interim crop insurance compensation to farmers who have enrolled under the crop insurance scheme and paid their premiums. He urged the Chief Minister to expedite the disbursement of drought relief to farmers. He requested the State government to ensure that the amount reaches all eligible farmers without delay and that the remaining amount is also released at the earliest. Mr. Patil also urged the Chief Minister to take up with the Maharashtra Government the issue of Karnataka’s share of water from the Ujani reservoir and get water released into the Bhima river course. He said that Maharashtra has failed to release Karnataka’s allocated share of 15 tmcft of water from the reservoir. Pointing out that the region is facing severe drought, he said that the Ujani reservoir reportedly holds around 60 tmcft of water in its dead storage.

• 1. Core Context & Background: MLA Allamprabhu Patil meets Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar recently and submits a memorandum seeking urgent financial assistance
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: MLA Allamprabhu Patil has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to release an additional grant of ₹5 crore to address the worsening drinking water crisis in Kalaburagi city where groundwater levels have reportedly depleted in nearly 80% of the areas, while borewells have gone dry. Mr. Patil met the Chief Minister in Bengaluru recently and submitted a memorandum seeking urgent financial assistance to tackle the situation. In the memorandum, the MLA also drew the Chief Minister’s attention to the extensive crop losses in the district due to drought and sought the early release of interim crop insurance compensation to farmers who have enrolled under the crop insurance scheme and paid their premiums. He urged the Chief Minister to expedite the disbursement of drought relief to farmers. Referring to the State government’s announcement of a minimum input subsidy of ₹5,000 to drought-affected farmers, he said that the first instalment of ₹2,500 has already been initiated through direct benefit transfer (DBT) to farmers bank accounts. He requested the State government to ensure that the amount reaches all eligible farmers without delay and that the remaining amount is also released at the earliest. Mr. Patil also urged the Chief Minister to take up with the Maharashtra Government the issue of Karnataka’s share of water from the Ujani reservoir and get water released into the Bhima river course. He said that Maharashtra has failed to release Karnataka’s allocated share of 15 tmcft of water from the reservoir. Pointing out that the region is facing severe drought, he said that the Ujani reservoir reportedly holds around 60 tmcft of water in its dead storage.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He urged Mr. Shivakumar to initiate discussions with the Maharashtra government and secure the release of at least 2 tmcft of water into the Bhima river course as an immediate measure.

articles.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted,’ COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing session

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat on Sunday (November 22, 2026) after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey. The main deal was rejected by a host of nations 44 hours after the summit's official close in a chaotic COP31 finale in the Turkish city of Antalya. "We will not endorse a cover decision... that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's Climate Minister, Darragh O'Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU Presidency. COP31 President Murat Kurum conceded the deal had failed to reach consensus. "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," he told the closing session. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war between the United States and Iran that has roiled the West Asia. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petrostates such as Saudi Arabia. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching "cover decision" to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the final proposal failed to mention coal, oil, and gas at all, plunging the summit into turmoil as it broke the record for the longest-ever UN climate conference.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future," the Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner told delegates.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:40:55 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted,’ COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing session

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat on Sunday (November 22, 2026) after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey. The main deal was rejected by a host of nations 44 hours after the summit's official close in a chaotic COP31 finale in the Turkish city of Antalya. "We will not endorse a cover decision... that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's Climate Minister, Darragh O'Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU Presidency. COP31 President Murat Kurum conceded the deal had failed to reach consensus. "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," he told the closing session. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war between the United States and Iran that has roiled the West Asia. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petrostates such as Saudi Arabia. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching "cover decision" to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the final proposal failed to mention coal, oil, and gas at all, plunging the summit into turmoil as it broke the record for the longest-ever UN climate conference.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future," the Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner told delegates.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: ‘I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted,’ COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing session
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat on Sunday (November 22, 2026) after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey. The main deal was rejected by a host of nations 44 hours after the summit's official close in a chaotic COP31 finale in the Turkish city of Antalya. "We will not endorse a cover decision... that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's Climate Minister, Darragh O'Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU Presidency. COP31 President Murat Kurum conceded the deal had failed to reach consensus. "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," he told the closing session. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war between the United States and Iran that has roiled the West Asia. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petrostates such as Saudi Arabia. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching "cover decision" to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the final proposal failed to mention coal, oil, and gas at all, plunging the summit into turmoil as it broke the record for the longest-ever UN climate conference.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future," the Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner told delegates.

articles.title: Congress corruption being exposed by its MLAs: KTR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao alleged widespread corruption in the Congress government, and said that its own legislators were exposing the commission-based system, citing the recent statements of Congress MLAs Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy and Anirudh Reddy.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Allegations relating to intimidation of industrialists and temple lands, including remarks by former Minister Konda Surekha, also pointed to the state of affairs in the government, he argued. Mr. Rama Rao, who was addressing a public meeting in Warangal on Sunday, declared that the countdown had begun for the Congress government and asserted that BRS president K. Chandrasekhar Rao would return as the Chief Minister in 2028. Questioning the Congress government’s claims of increasing social security pensions, he said it had removed 4.71 lakh existing beneficiaries while adding only 4.63 lakh new beneficiaries. The BRS MLA dismissed Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s claim on empowering women, and reminded that Congress had promised a monthly assistance of ₹2,500 to women but had failed to implement it even after 36 months in office. According to him, the accumulated dues amounted to ₹85,500 for each eligible woman. He also referred to other promises like one tola of gold under Kalyana Lakshmi, scooters for girl students and financial assistance ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹10 lakh for students. “If the promises are fulfilled and women are made financially secure, I will quit politics permanently,” he said. Targeting Mr. Revanth Reddy, he said the Chief Minister was more interested in making personal remarks against KCR than addressing farmers’ problems, unemployment, drought and industrial development. KTR also accused the Congress government of putting Warangal’s development on hold over the last three years. The BRS government had sanctioned six government medical colleges and the 24-storey super-speciality hospital with 2,250 beds and 35 medical departments. Similarly, the BRS government had brought IT companies and the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park, generating employment for local youth, he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He accused the government of failing to utilise Godavari waters effectively and alleged that poor management of the Devadula pumping stations and Kannepalli motors was affecting irrigation.

📰 Congress corruption being exposed by its MLAs: KTR

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:23:12 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao alleged widespread corruption in the Congress government, and said that its own legislators were exposing the commission-based system, citing the recent statements of Congress MLAs Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy and Anirudh Reddy.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Allegations relating to intimidation of industrialists and temple lands, including remarks by former Minister Konda Surekha, also pointed to the state of affairs in the government, he argued. Mr. Rama Rao, who was addressing a public meeting in Warangal on Sunday, declared that the countdown had begun for the Congress government and asserted that BRS president K. Chandrasekhar Rao would return as the Chief Minister in 2028. Questioning the Congress government’s claims of increasing social security pensions, he said it had removed 4.71 lakh existing beneficiaries while adding only 4.63 lakh new beneficiaries. The BRS MLA dismissed Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s claim on empowering women, and reminded that Congress had promised a monthly assistance of ₹2,500 to women but had failed to implement it even after 36 months in office. According to him, the accumulated dues amounted to ₹85,500 for each eligible woman. He also referred to other promises like one tola of gold under Kalyana Lakshmi, scooters for girl students and financial assistance ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹10 lakh for students. “If the promises are fulfilled and women are made financially secure, I will quit politics permanently,” he said. Targeting Mr. Revanth Reddy, he said the Chief Minister was more interested in making personal remarks against KCR than addressing farmers’ problems, unemployment, drought and industrial development. KTR also accused the Congress government of putting Warangal’s development on hold over the last three years. The BRS government had sanctioned six government medical colleges and the 24-storey super-speciality hospital with 2,250 beds and 35 medical departments. Similarly, the BRS government had brought IT companies and the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park, generating employment for local youth, he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He accused the government of failing to utilise Godavari waters effectively and alleged that poor management of the Devadula pumping stations and Kannepalli motors was affecting irrigation.

articles.title: Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for ASHA workers, Ashok tells CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to walk the talk by increasing the honorarium of protesting ASHA workers as per the Congress party’s pre-poll promise.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Taking to social media, Mr. Ashok accused the Congress of luring ASHA workers to support the party ahead of the Assembly elections by promising an increase in honorarium and forgetting them after coming to power. “I want to ask Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, his predecessor Siddaramaiah and All India Congress Committee general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala if it was not true that they had held a separate meeting with representatives of the ASHA workers ahead of the polls and promised them a hike in honorarium?,” Mr. Ashok said in the social media post. He said, “These Congress leaders take the name of the Constitution for everything. If they are true to their conscience, let them swear by the name of the Constitution that they did not make any pre-poll promise on increasing the honorarium of the ASHA workers.” “You came to power by luring women voters through such promises and visiting their doorsteps. But now you have forgotten these women after coming to power,” he remarked. “You describe women as goddesses before elections, but after coming to power, you get irritated if these ASHA workers remind you about your pending promise,” Mr. Ashok ridiculed. Taking serious exception to the government citing a lack of funds to implement ASHA workers’ demands, he wondered why the government did not think of financial burden when it appointed its party workers to various boards and corporations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to the Chief Minister’s visit to Japan, Mr. Ashok further remarked that the Chief Minister was enjoying his foreign trip when ASHA workers were suffering in the name of protest.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for ASHA workers, Ashok tells CM

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:20:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to walk the talk by increasing the honorarium of protesting ASHA workers as per the Congress party’s pre-poll promise.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Taking to social media, Mr. Ashok accused the Congress of luring ASHA workers to support the party ahead of the Assembly elections by promising an increase in honorarium and forgetting them after coming to power. “I want to ask Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, his predecessor Siddaramaiah and All India Congress Committee general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala if it was not true that they had held a separate meeting with representatives of the ASHA workers ahead of the polls and promised them a hike in honorarium?,” Mr. Ashok said in the social media post. He said, “These Congress leaders take the name of the Constitution for everything. If they are true to their conscience, let them swear by the name of the Constitution that they did not make any pre-poll promise on increasing the honorarium of the ASHA workers.” “You came to power by luring women voters through such promises and visiting their doorsteps. But now you have forgotten these women after coming to power,” he remarked. “You describe women as goddesses before elections, but after coming to power, you get irritated if these ASHA workers remind you about your pending promise,” Mr. Ashok ridiculed. Taking serious exception to the government citing a lack of funds to implement ASHA workers’ demands, he wondered why the government did not think of financial burden when it appointed its party workers to various boards and corporations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to the Chief Minister’s visit to Japan, Mr. Ashok further remarked that the Chief Minister was enjoying his foreign trip when ASHA workers were suffering in the name of protest.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Legislative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Legislative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Opposition (Noun)
विरोध — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Opposition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for ASHA workers, Ashok tells CM", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for ASHA ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for AS' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for AS' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R." (Hinglish Arth: विधानसभा में विपक्ष के नेता आर.)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Walk the talk by increasing honorarium for ASHA workers, Ashok tells CM"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Ashok further remarked that the Chief Minister was enjoying his foreign trip when ASHA workers were suffering in the name of protest.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Ashok further remarked that the Chief Minister was enjoying his foreign trip when ASHA workers were suffering in the name of protest." (Hinglish Arth: अशोक ने आगे टिप्पणी की कि जब आशा कार्यकर्ता विरोध के नाम पर पीड़ित हो रहे थे तो मुख्यमंत्री अपनी विदेश यात्रा का आनंद ले रहे थे।)

articles.title: Rajasthan Congress chief credits organisational strength for panchayat polls victory
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: State Congress Chief Govind Singh Dotasra said that while anti-incumbency against the BJP government contributed to the Congress's victory

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rajasthan unit president of the Congress, Govind Singh Dotasra, attributed the party’s victory in the recent Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad elections to two major reasons: anti-incumbency against the Bharatiya Janata Party’s “ parchi sarkar ” (a government working on slips of instruction coming from Delhi) and the Congress breaking from its tradition of handing over a “ lifafa ” (envelope) to State leaders to pick the candidates of their choice. Speaking to The Hindu over the phone from his residence in Sikar on Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning, Mr. Dotasra asserted that the message from Rajasthan is “loud and clear”. “People’s voice is the ultimate power in a democracy,” he said. According to him, the people were speaking against a combination of factors: the government’s failure to control crime and corruption, and the centralisation of power in Delhi. “The Ministers in the Bhajan Lal [Sharma] government have no power; either Delhi decides or the bureaucracy,” he said. The Congress’s attack on the government has centred on these themes. Mocking the BJP’s slogan of a “double-engine” government, Mr. Dotasra described the administration as a “quadruple-engine” government, counting the bureaucracy and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) as two additional engines that make it an unwieldy arrangement. Beyond the rhetoric, however, Mr. Dotasra sounded almost relieved when he asserted that the Congress had managed to maintain discipline. “ Varna Congress main sabse pehle anushasan bhang ho jaata hai (Otherwise, discipline is the first thing to break down in the Congress.),” he said. The discipline, he said, was reflected both in the party’s messaging and in keeping the organisation active on the ground. He listed several firsts achieved by the Rajasthan Congress ahead of other State units. Rajasthan was the first State to complete the appointment of ‘mandal committees’, a new intermediary tier introduced between booth-level and block-level committees after the Congress’s Udaipur Chintan Shivir in May 2022. There are 2,200 mandals in Rajasthan, each with about 31 members, averaging 11 mandal committees per Assembly constituency. “We would have regular meetings of these mandal committees. Any functionary who did not show up for three consecutive meetings would be automatically removed,” Mr. Dotasra said, underlining that this ensured a continuous process of weeding out non-serious functionaries. Moreover, soon after the party’s defeat in 2023, the Pradesh Congress Committee appointed coordinators for each Assembly segment, he said. Apart from organisational work, he also credited collective leadership. “We spoke in one voice,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Dotasra has taken to shutting down sloganeering in favour of individual leaders at election rallies. For example, at a public meeting in Jodhpur in August, when former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot arrived, the crowd began raising slogans of “Ashok Gehlot chauthi baar ” (Ashok Gehlot for a fourth time), cheering for his return as Chief Minister in the 2028 elections. Mr. Dotasra intervened to stop the slogans, tersely asking the crowd to work for the Congress instead. “Discipline cannot be maintained by speaking only sweetly; one has to occasionally serve a bitter dose,” he said.

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Rajasthan Congress chief credits organisational strength for panchayat polls victory"?
options: Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
“Discipline cannot be maintained by speaking only sweetly; one has to occasionally serve a bitter dose,” he said.
Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: “Discipline cannot be maintained by speaking only sweetly; one has to occasionally serve a bitter dose,” he said.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“Discipline cannot be maintained by speaking only sweetly; one has to occasionally serve a bitter dose,” he said." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा, "केवल मीठा बोलने से अनुशासन कायम नहीं रखा जा सकता, कभी-कभी कड़वी खुराक भी परोसनी पड़ती है।")

hinglishTracks.en: State Congress Chief Govind Singh Dotasra said that while anti-incumbency against the BJP government contributed to the Congress's victory
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — प्रदेश कांग्रेस प्रमुख गोविंद सिंह डोटासरा ने कहा कि भाजपा सरकार के खिलाफ सत्ता विरोधी लहर ने कांग्रेस की जीत में योगदान दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Rajasthan unit president of the Congress, Govind Singh Dotasra, attributed the party’s victory in the recent Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad elections to two major reasons: anti-incumbency against the Bharatiya Janata Party’s “ parchi sarkar ” (a government working on slips of instruction coming from Delhi) and the Congress breaking from its tradition of handing over a “ lifafa ” (envelope) to State leaders to pick the candidates of their choice.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कांग्रेस की राजस्थान इकाई के अध्यक्ष गोविंद सिंह डोटासरा ने हाल के पंचायत समिति और जिला परिषद चुनावों में पार्टी की जीत के लिए दो प्रमुख कारणों को जिम्मेदार ठहराया: भारतीय जनता पार्टी की "पर्ची सरकार" (दिल्ली से आने वाली निर्देश की पर्चियों पर काम करने वाली सरकार) के खिलाफ सत्ता विरोधी लहर और कांग्रेस द्वारा अपने उम्मीदवारों को चुनने के लिए राज्य के नेताओं को "लिफाफा" (लिफाफा) सौंपने की अपनी परंपरा को तोड़ना।।

hinglishTracks.en: Speaking to The Hindu over the phone from his residence in Sikar on Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning, Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — रविवार (नवंबर 22, 2026) सुबह सीकर स्थित अपने आवास से फोन पर द हिंदू से बात करते हुए, श्री.।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra asserted that the message from Rajasthan is “loud and clear”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — डोटासरा ने जोर देकर कहा कि राजस्थान का संदेश "जोरदार और स्पष्ट" है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “People’s voice is the ultimate power in a democracy,” he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उन्होंने कहा, "लोकतंत्र में लोगों की आवाज ही सर्वोच्च शक्ति है।"।

hinglishTracks.en: According to him, the people were speaking against a combination of factors: the government’s failure to control crime and corruption, and the centralisation of power in Delhi.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उनके अनुसार, लोग कारकों के संयोजन के खिलाफ बोल रहे थे: अपराध और भ्रष्टाचार को नियंत्रित करने में सरकार की विफलता, और दिल्ली में सत्ता का केंद्रीकरण।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Centralisation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: केंद्रीकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Centralisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: “The Ministers in the Bhajan Lal [Sharma] government have no power; either Delhi decides or the bureaucracy,” he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने कहा, "भजन लाल (शर्मा) सरकार के मंत्रियों के पास कोई शक्ति नहीं है; या तो दिल्ली निर्णय लेती है या नौकरशाही।"।

hinglishTracks.en: The Congress’s attack on the government has centred on these themes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सरकार पर कांग्रेस का हमला इन्हीं विषयों पर केंद्रित है.।

hinglishTracks.en: Mocking the BJP’s slogan of a “double-engine” government, Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — भाजपा के "डबल इंजन" सरकार के नारे का मज़ाक उड़ाते हुए, श्री.।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra described the administration as a “quadruple-engine” government, counting the bureaucracy and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) as two additional engines that make it an unwieldy arrangement.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — डोटासरा ने प्रशासन को "चार इंजन वाली" सरकार के रूप में वर्णित किया, नौकरशाही और राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ (आरएसएस) को दो अतिरिक्त इंजनों के रूप में गिना जो इसे एक बोझिल व्यवस्था बनाते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Beyond the rhetoric, however, Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालाँकि, बयानबाजी से परे, श्रीमान...।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra sounded almost relieved when he asserted that the Congress had managed to maintain discipline.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — डोटासरा ने लगभग राहत महसूस की जब उन्होंने कहा कि कांग्रेस अनुशासन बनाए रखने में कामयाब रही है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “ Varna Congress main sabse pehle anushasan bhang ho jaata hai (Otherwise, discipline is the first thing to break down in the Congress.),” he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — उन्होंने कहा, “वरना कांग्रेस में सबसे पहले अनुशासन भंग हो जाता है।”।

hinglishTracks.en: The discipline, he said, was reflected both in the party’s messaging and in keeping the organisation active on the ground.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने कहा, अनुशासन पार्टी के संदेश और जमीन पर संगठन को सक्रिय रखने, दोनों में परिलक्षित होता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Organisational' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Organisational' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: He listed several firsts achieved by the Rajasthan Congress ahead of other State units.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उन्होंने अन्य राज्य इकाइयों की तुलना में राजस्थान कांग्रेस द्वारा पहली बार हासिल की गई कई उपलब्धियां गिनाईं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Rajasthan was the first State to complete the appointment of ‘mandal committees’, a new intermediary tier introduced between booth-level and block-level committees after the Congress’s Udaipur Chintan Shivir in May 2022.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — राजस्थान 'मंडल समितियों' की नियुक्ति पूरी करने वाला पहला राज्य था, मई 2022 में कांग्रेस के उदयपुर चिंतन शिविर के बाद बूथ-स्तरीय और ब्लॉक-स्तरीय समितियों के बीच एक नया मध्यस्थ स्तर पेश किया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: There are 2,200 mandals in Rajasthan, each with about 31 members, averaging 11 mandal committees per Assembly constituency.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — राजस्थान में 2,200 मंडल हैं, प्रत्येक में लगभग 31 सदस्य हैं, प्रति विधानसभा क्षेत्र में औसतन 11 मंडल समितियाँ हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: “We would have regular meetings of these mandal committees.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — “हम इन मंडल समितियों की नियमित बैठकें करेंगे।।

hinglishTracks.en: Any functionary who did not show up for three consecutive meetings would be automatically removed,” Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — जो भी पदाधिकारी लगातार तीन बैठकों में नहीं आएगा, उसे स्वत: हटा दिया जाएगा।''।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra said, underlining that this ensured a continuous process of weeding out non-serious functionaries.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — डोटासरा ने यह रेखांकित करते हुए कहा कि इससे गैर-गंभीर पदाधिकारियों को बाहर करने की एक सतत प्रक्रिया सुनिश्चित हुई।।

hinglishTracks.en: Moreover, soon after the party’s defeat in 2023, the Pradesh Congress Committee appointed coordinators for each Assembly segment, he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इसके अलावा, 2023 में पार्टी की हार के तुरंत बाद, प्रदेश कांग्रेस कमेटी ने प्रत्येक विधानसभा क्षेत्र के लिए समन्वयक नियुक्त किए, उन्होंने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: Apart from organisational work, he also credited collective leadership.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने संगठनात्मक कार्यों के अलावा सामूहिक नेतृत्व को भी श्रेय दिया.। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Organisational' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Organisational' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: “We spoke in one voice,” he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — उन्होंने कहा, ''हमने एक स्वर में बात की.''।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra has taken to shutting down sloganeering in favour of individual leaders at election rallies.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — डोटासरा ने चुनावी रैलियों में व्यक्तिगत नेताओं के पक्ष में नारेबाजी बंद करने का निर्णय लिया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: For example, at a public meeting in Jodhpur in August, when former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot arrived, the crowd began raising slogans of “Ashok Gehlot chauthi baar ” (Ashok Gehlot for a fourth time), cheering for his return as Chief Minister in the 2028 elections.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उदाहरण के लिए, अगस्त में जोधपुर में एक सार्वजनिक बैठक में, जब पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अशोक गहलोत पहुंचे, तो भीड़ ने 2028 के चुनावों में मुख्यमंत्री के रूप में उनकी वापसी के लिए जयकार करते हुए "अशोक गहलोत चौथी बार" (चौथी बार) के नारे लगाने शुरू कर दिए।।

hinglishTracks.en: Dotasra intervened to stop the slogans, tersely asking the crowd to work for the Congress instead.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — डोटासरा ने नारेबाज़ी रोकने के लिए हस्तक्षेप किया और भीड़ से कांग्रेस के लिए काम करने को कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: “Discipline cannot be maintained by speaking only sweetly; one has to occasionally serve a bitter dose,” he said.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने कहा, "केवल मीठा बोलने से अनुशासन कायम नहीं रखा जा सकता, कभी-कभी कड़वी खुराक भी परोसनी पड़ती है।"।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Rajasthan Congress chief credits organisational strength for panchayat polls victory

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:15:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: State Congress Chief Govind Singh Dotasra said that while anti-incumbency against the BJP government contributed to the Congress's victory

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rajasthan unit president of the Congress, Govind Singh Dotasra, attributed the party’s victory in the recent Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad elections to two major reasons: anti-incumbency against the Bharatiya Janata Party’s “ parchi sarkar ” (a government working on slips of instruction coming from Delhi) and the Congress breaking from its tradition of handing over a “ lifafa ” (envelope) to State leaders to pick the candidates of their choice. Speaking to The Hindu over the phone from his residence in Sikar on Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning, Mr. Dotasra asserted that the message from Rajasthan is “loud and clear”. “People’s voice is the ultimate power in a democracy,” he said. According to him, the people were speaking against a combination of factors: the government’s failure to control crime and corruption, and the centralisation of power in Delhi. “The Ministers in the Bhajan Lal [Sharma] government have no power; either Delhi decides or the bureaucracy,” he said. The Congress’s attack on the government has centred on these themes. Mocking the BJP’s slogan of a “double-engine” government, Mr. Dotasra described the administration as a “quadruple-engine” government, counting the bureaucracy and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) as two additional engines that make it an unwieldy arrangement. Beyond the rhetoric, however, Mr. Dotasra sounded almost relieved when he asserted that the Congress had managed to maintain discipline. “ Varna Congress main sabse pehle anushasan bhang ho jaata hai (Otherwise, discipline is the first thing to break down in the Congress.),” he said. The discipline, he said, was reflected both in the party’s messaging and in keeping the organisation active on the ground. He listed several firsts achieved by the Rajasthan Congress ahead of other State units. Rajasthan was the first State to complete the appointment of ‘mandal committees’, a new intermediary tier introduced between booth-level and block-level committees after the Congress’s Udaipur Chintan Shivir in May 2022. There are 2,200 mandals in Rajasthan, each with about 31 members, averaging 11 mandal committees per Assembly constituency. “We would have regular meetings of these mandal committees. Any functionary who did not show up for three consecutive meetings would be automatically removed,” Mr. Dotasra said, underlining that this ensured a continuous process of weeding out non-serious functionaries. Moreover, soon after the party’s defeat in 2023, the Pradesh Congress Committee appointed coordinators for each Assembly segment, he said. articles.title: From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 140-year-old heritage building to get a new lease of life
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The heritage building, which formerly housed the Devanahalli taluk office, has been officially handed over by the Revenue Department to the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage. Officials said that they will restore the building and convert it into a museum for tourists, school and college students to visit.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The building is more than 140 years old. The pictures available with The Hindu of the building show a carving on the wall that the building was constructed in 1880. Speaking to The Hindu , B. G. Gurusiddaiah, a historian and resident of Devanahalli, who spearheaded the move to restore the building, said, “The taluk office moved to Mini Vidhana Soudha in 2012. Since then, the old building has remained vacant for many years. This came to my notice in 2022 and from then, I have approached Bengaluru Rural commissioner, Tourism Minister and other officials concerned seeking permission to hand over the building to Archaeology Department.” Recently, an official order was issued by the Revenue Department handing over the building to the Department of Archaeology. The building cannot be leased or transferred, or encroached. Meanwhile, a senior official from the Archaeology Department said, “The building is quite old and before restoring it, we need to study on how it can be done. We want to establish a museum here. Our team recently visited the building in Devanahalli and surveyed it. A detailed report will be submitted to the government for funds.” The official added, “We may include a non-profit organisation that can help us restore the interiors and exterior of the building. However, the old structure will not be disturbed. This heritage building showcases English style of architecture including steep roofs covered with Mangalore tiles, pointed arches and wide pillars. There are also two old stones at the entrance of the taluk office including Mastigallu and Veeragallu which may belong to eighth century.” The museum will display details of stone inscriptions found in and around Devanahalli, the famous chakota fruit that has earned GI tag, historical monuments and about the famous writers who were born in Devanahalli. These writers include D. V. Gundappa, K. S. Nisar Ahmed, Kamala Hampana and a few others.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The museum will definitely bring large crowd to because of the presence of fort and a few other places in the taluk. It can be a tourist spot or a place of outing for those living in the city. Avatihalli, a village where forefathers of Nadaprabhu Kempegowda settled, is also located close to the museum. There are also other places like Avati betta, Avati lake and others. After visiting these places, people will spend some time in the museum,” Mr. Gurusiddaiah said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 140-year-old heritage building to get a new lease of life

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:12:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The heritage building, which formerly housed the Devanahalli taluk office, has been officially handed over by the Revenue Department to the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage. Officials said that they will restore the building and convert it into a museum for tourists, school and college students to visit.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The building is more than 140 years old. The pictures available with The Hindu of the building show a carving on the wall that the building was constructed in 1880. Speaking to The Hindu , B. G. Gurusiddaiah, a historian and resident of Devanahalli, who spearheaded the move to restore the building, said, “The taluk office moved to Mini Vidhana Soudha in 2012. Since then, the old building has remained vacant for many years. This came to my notice in 2022 and from then, I have approached Bengaluru Rural commissioner, Tourism Minister and other officials concerned seeking permission to hand over the building to Archaeology Department.” Recently, an official order was issued by the Revenue Department handing over the building to the Department of Archaeology. The building cannot be leased or transferred, or encroached. Meanwhile, a senior official from the Archaeology Department said, “The building is quite old and before restoring it, we need to study on how it can be done. We want to establish a museum here. Our team recently visited the building in Devanahalli and surveyed it. A detailed report will be submitted to the government for funds.” The official added, “We may include a non-profit organisation that can help us restore the interiors and exterior of the building. However, the old structure will not be disturbed. This heritage building showcases English style of architecture including steep roofs covered with Mangalore tiles, pointed arches and wide pillars. There are also two old stones at the entrance of the taluk office including Mastigallu and Veeragallu which may belong to eighth century.” The museum will display details of stone inscriptions found in and around Devanahalli, the famous chakota fruit that has earned GI tag, historical monuments and about the famous writers who were born in Devanahalli. These writers include D. V. Gundappa, K. S. Nisar Ahmed, Kamala Hampana and a few others.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The museum will definitely bring large crowd to because of the presence of fort and a few other places in the taluk. It can be a tourist spot or a place of outing for those living in the city. Avatihalli, a village where forefathers of Nadaprabhu Kempegowda settled, is also located close to the museum. There are also other places like Avati betta, Avati lake and others. After visiting these places, people will spend some time in the museum,” Mr. Gurusiddaiah said.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Historical' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

A. The heritage building, which formerly housed the Devanahalli taluk office, has been officially handed over by the Revenue Department to the...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 140-y' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 14' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 14' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The heritage building, which formerly housed the Devanahalli taluk office, has been officially handed over by the Revenue Department to the..." (Hinglish Arth: विरासत भवन, जिसमें पहले देवनहल्ली तालुक कार्यालय हुआ करता था, को राजस्व विभाग द्वारा आधिकारिक तौर पर पुरातत्व, संग्रहालय और विरासत विभाग को सौंप दिया गया है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "From taluk office to museum: Devanahalli’s 140-year-old heritage building to get a new lease of life"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "After visiting these places, people will spend some time in the museum,” Mr." (Hinglish Arth: इन स्थानों पर जाने के बाद लोग कुछ समय संग्रहालय में बिताएंगे।'')

articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said. Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia. "The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied. Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added. The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X. OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties. The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises. The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026. “Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026. “Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — रात करीब दो बजे खार्तूम हवाईअड्डे के आसपास के इलाके और शहर के अन्य हिस्सों में विस्फोटों की आवाजें सुनी गईं।।

चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — (0000-0230 जीएमटी)।।

hinglishTracks.en: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — एक प्रत्यक्षदर्शी ने कहा कि ड्रोन हमले ने एक घर को पूरी तरह से नष्ट कर दिया, जबकि सूडानी सेना के एक सूत्र ने कहा कि ड्रोन इथियोपिया से लॉन्च किए गए थे।।

hinglishTracks.en: OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger.

hinglishTracks.en: The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — सहायता कर्मियों का अनुमान है कि अर्धसैनिक रैपिड सपोर्ट फोर्स (आरएसएफ) और सूडानी सेना के बीच अप्रैल 2023 में शुरू हुए संघर्ष में 2,00,000 से अधिक लोग मारे गए और दुनिया में सबसे बड़ा भूख और विस्थापन संकट पैदा हो गया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Displacement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: विस्थापन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Displacement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने दोनों पक्षों द्वारा ड्रोन के बड़े पैमाने पर उपयोग की बार-बार आलोचना की है, जिससे 2026 की पहली छमाही में 1,100 से अधिक लोग मारे गए।।

hinglishTracks.en: “Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने पिछले सप्ताह कहा था, "इस साल मारे गए सैकड़ों बच्चों में से दो-तिहाई ड्रोन हमलों में मारे गए या घायल हुए।"।

hinglishTracks.en: A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — कुछ दिन पहले सूडानी सेना के ड्रोन हमले में पश्चिमी कोर्डोफन गांव में चार बच्चों सहित 15 लोगों की मौत हो गई थी, क्योंकि सेना ने आरएसएफ से क्षेत्र को वापस लेते हुए राज्य में घुसपैठ की थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — प्रतिद्वंद्वी ताकतें पिछले साल से संसाधन संपन्न दक्षिणी कोर्डोफन क्षेत्र पर नियंत्रण के लिए संघर्ष कर रही हैं, जो सेना के कब्जे वाले केंद्र और पूर्व को आरएसएफ-नियंत्रित दारफुर से जोड़ता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — हाल के महीनों में, सेना और आरएसएफ दोनों ने अपने लड़ाकू विमानों को जोखिम में डाले बिना सैकड़ों किलोमीटर दूर लक्ष्य पर हमला करने में सक्षम ड्रोन पर भरोसा किया है।।

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:58:28 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said. Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia. "The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied. Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added. The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X. OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties. The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises. The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026. “Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said. Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia. "The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied. Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added. The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X. OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties. The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises. The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026. “Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

articles.title: Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam city. Members of Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, marched from the RK Beach bus stop to the Bhagat Singh statue, raising slogans and handing out pamphlets to passers-by.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: G. Kantarao, treasurer of the organisation, said the government had not said how many jobs would be created, even as data centre capacity rose to over six gigawatts. He alleged that the government was serving corporate interests by allotting hills at Rushikonda and Yendada, and those belonging to the Simhachalam Devasthanam, to private firms. He demanded that all permissions given to these corporations be cancelled. “If the government does not cancel them, we will turn this into a people’s movement,” he said. The rally ended at the Bhagat Singh statue on purpose, Mr. Kantarao said. Just as Bhagat Singh had turned the course of the freedom struggle, the organisers hoped to turn the course of this agitation. Sai Teja, district president of the Students’ Federation of India, alleged that the “Stop Vizag Data Centre” social media account had been taken down three times, most recently two days before the rally. “Why is the government so afraid?” he asked. He said development should be sustainable and create jobs. Dhyuti, a research scientist and environmentalist, said the campaigners wanted clear information on health hazards, cooling methods and skilled jobs. Visakhapatnam was prone to drought and could not spare water and land for data centres, she said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Green Visakha secretary M. Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:24:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam city. Members of Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, marched from the RK Beach bus stop to the Bhagat Singh statue, raising slogans and handing out pamphlets to passers-by.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: G. Kantarao, treasurer of the organisation, said the government had not said how many jobs would be created, even as data centre capacity rose to over six gigawatts. He alleged that the government was serving corporate interests by allotting hills at Rushikonda and Yendada, and those belonging to the Simhachalam Devasthanam, to private firms. He demanded that all permissions given to these corporations be cancelled. “If the government does not cancel them, we will turn this into a people’s movement,” he said. The rally ended at the Bhagat Singh statue on purpose, Mr. Kantarao said. Just as Bhagat Singh had turned the course of the freedom struggle, the organisers hoped to turn the course of this agitation. Sai Teja, district president of the Students’ Federation of India, alleged that the “Stop Vizag Data Centre” social media account had been taken down three times, most recently two days before the rally. “Why is the government so afraid?” he asked. He said development should be sustainable and create jobs. Dhyuti, a research scientist and environmentalist, said the campaigners wanted clear information on health hazards, cooling methods and skilled jobs. Visakhapatnam was prone to drought and could not spare water and land for data centres, she said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Green Visakha secretary M. Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Permissibility (Noun)
कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।
✓ Syn: Admissibility, Legality, Allowance  |  ✖ Ant: Prohibition, Ban, Illegality
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against d' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against d' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam..." (Hinglish Arth: रविवार शाम आगंतुकों से खचाखच भरी बीच रोड, विशाखापत्तनम शहर और उसके आसपास बन रहे डेटा सेंटरों के खिलाफ एक अभियान की पृष्ठभूमि बन गई।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part." (Hinglish Arth: चन्द्रशेखर, पर्यावरण कार्यकर्ता जयश्री हतांगडी और तिरूपति राव और मानवाधिकार मंच की अनुराधा ने हिस्सा लिया।)

articles.title: Walkathon stresses importance of natural childbirth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Ensuring that childbirth is safe, dignified and empowering for a mother is a collective responsibility, said Andhra Pradesh Transport Department Employees Association, Zone-II, president M. Rajubabu.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Inaugurating a walkathon, organised in response to a call by the Society of Midwives India to promote awareness of natural childbirth, in Vijayawada on Sunday, November 22, Mr. Rajubabu emphasised the importance of maternal health, proper nutrition, regular antenatal check-ups and family support. He highlighted that emotional well-being, confidence and a supportive family environment are as important as medical care during pregnancy. He described the walkathon as more than a fitness activity, calling it a movement for maternal health, safe childbirth, women’s dignity and healthier future generations. He urged students and youth to spread awareness in every community. Government Nursing College principal S. Naga Seshamma said that the initiative aimed to promote natural childbirth, reduce medically unnecessary caesarean deliveries and highlighted the vital role of trained midwives. She stressed that caesarean sections must be respected wherever medically necessary, with delivery decisions guided by the health and safety of mother and baby.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Students from the Government Nursing College, Pinnamaneni Siddhartha Nursing College and BC and SC hostels enthusiastically participated. Faculty members, association representatives and women’s organisations also attended.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Walkathon stresses importance of natural childbirth

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:11:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Ensuring that childbirth is safe, dignified and empowering for a mother is a collective responsibility, said Andhra Pradesh Transport Department Employees Association, Zone-II, president M. Rajubabu.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Inaugurating a walkathon, organised in response to a call by the Society of Midwives India to promote awareness of natural childbirth, in Vijayawada on Sunday, November 22, Mr. Rajubabu emphasised the importance of maternal health, proper nutrition, regular antenatal check-ups and family support. He highlighted that emotional well-being, confidence and a supportive family environment are as important as medical care during pregnancy. He described the walkathon as more than a fitness activity, calling it a movement for maternal health, safe childbirth, women’s dignity and healthier future generations. He urged students and youth to spread awareness in every community. Government Nursing College principal S. Naga Seshamma said that the initiative aimed to promote natural childbirth, reduce medically unnecessary caesarean deliveries and highlighted the vital role of trained midwives. She stressed that caesarean sections must be respected wherever medically necessary, with delivery decisions guided by the health and safety of mother and baby.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Students from the Government Nursing College, Pinnamaneni Siddhartha Nursing College and BC and SC hostels enthusiastically participated. Faculty members, association representatives and women’s organisations also attended.

B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Walkathon stresses importance of natural childbi' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Walkathon stresses importance of natural chil' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Walkathon stresses importance of natural chil' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: State BJP chief claims Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not language, as Bengali-speaking Hindus are now being persecuted and bearing the consequences of Partition

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh . “Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons. Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language. “Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the fundamental question at that time should have been the protection of people and the creation of a democratic environment. Instead, the leadership surrendered to religious fundamentalism, he said. Claiming that the wounds of Partition continued to haunt the subcontinent, the BJP leader said that it was religious minorities, particularly Hindus in Bangladesh, who were bearing the consequences. Blaming Partition on Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi, Mr. Bhattacharya claimed that had Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose become independent India’s first Prime Minister, he would never have accepted the two-nation theory or allowed the subcontinent to be divided into India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The remarks by the West Bengal BJP leader come at a time when fresh political tensions have erupted in Bangladesh. Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. Ms. Hasina has announced that she is keen to return to Bangladesh.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:04:12 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: State BJP chief claims Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not language, as Bengali-speaking Hindus are now being persecuted and bearing the consequences of Partition

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh . “Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons. Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language. “Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the fundamental question at that time should have been the protection of people and the creation of a democratic environment. Instead, the leadership surrendered to religious fundamentalism, he said. Claiming that the wounds of Partition continued to haunt the subcontinent, the BJP leader said that it was religious minorities, particularly Hindus in Bangladesh, who were bearing the consequences. Blaming Partition on Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi, Mr. Bhattacharya claimed that had Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose become independent India’s first Prime Minister, he would never have accepted the two-nation theory or allowed the subcontinent to be divided into India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The remarks by the West Bengal BJP leader come at a time when fresh political tensions have erupted in Bangladesh. Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. Ms. Hasina has announced that she is keen to return to Bangladesh.

पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
