✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Investment (Adjective)
निवेश — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Investment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Instrument (Adjective)
यंत्र — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Instrument' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultu' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultu' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports..." (Hinglish Arth: ऑल इंडिया जेम एंड ज्वैलरी डोमेस्टिक काउंसिल (जीजेसी) ने तर्क दिया कि सोने के आभूषण क्षेत्र अर्थव्यवस्था में लगभग 7-8% योगदान देता है और लाखों आजीविका का समर्थन करता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and..." (Hinglish Arth: “₹10 लाख करोड़ के उद्योग के रूप में, भारतीय आभूषण क्षेत्र को अधिक पारदर्शिता, मूल्य सृजन और राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकताओं के साथ संरेखण के साथ जिम्मेदारी से बढ़ना जारी रखना चाहिए – भारत की आर्थिक देशभक्ति के साथ संतुलन बनाना चाहिए।”)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसा कोई कारण नहीं है कि भारत के बाहर के किसी व्यक्ति का मूल्यांकन उपनिवेशवाद माना जाए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — फिर भी प्रधान मंत्री की आर्थिक सलाहकार परिषद में क्रमशः सदस्य, संयुक्त निदेशक और एक युवा पेशेवर, संजीव सान्याल, सात्विक देव और पायल शर्मा द्वारा व्यापक रूप से बहस किए गए लेख में यह आरोप लगाया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — शोधकर्ता एक अध्ययन लिखते हैं और इसे एक पांडुलिपि के रूप में एक पत्रिका में जमा करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — पत्रिका के संपादक पांडुलिपि का मूल्यांकन करते हैं और इसे क्षेत्र के अन्य विशेषज्ञों को भेजते हैं और पूछते हैं कि क्या काम प्रकाशन लायक है, या इसे संशोधित करने या अस्वीकार करने की आवश्यकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यदि जर्नल पेपर को स्वीकार कर लेता है, तो इसे प्रकाशित किया जाएगा, दुनिया भर के वैज्ञानिकों के ध्यान में लाया जाएगा और इसका एक स्थायी रिकॉर्ड संरक्षित किया जाएगा।।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Indian science needs fewer borders

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:51:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administrative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administrative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Irrespective (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Irrespective' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Indian science needs fewer borders", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Indian science needs fewer borders' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Indian science needs fewer borders' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Indian science needs fewer borders' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and..." (Hinglish Arth: अनुसंधान संस्थानों को समय पर वित्त पोषण, बेहतर शिक्षण प्रोत्साहन, अधिक स्वायत्तता, नेतृत्व नियंत्रण, बदले की भावना के खिलाफ सुरक्षा उपाय और कम प्रशासनिक बोझ की आवश्यकता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Indian science needs fewer borders"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved." (Hinglish Arth: यदि जर्नल पेपर को स्वीकार कर लेता है, तो इसे प्रकाशित किया जाएगा, दुनिया भर के वैज्ञानिकों के ध्यान में लाया जाएगा और इसका एक स्थायी रिकॉर्ड संरक्षित किया जाएगा।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / France / space programme / defence equipment / Artificial Intelligence / economy / security measures / United Nations / technology (general) / oceans / climate change / ISRO / water / summit / weather science / science (general) / law

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. articles.title: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:00:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

प्रामाणिकता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Authenticity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Apartment (Adjective)
अपार्टमेंट — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Apartment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Explosion (Noun)
विस्फोट — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Explosion' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes' should be permanently discontinued.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: climate change / Turkey / politics / Australia / electricity production and distribution / energy and resource / European Union / solar / India / China / carbon emissions / population / economy / carbon capture and sequestration / Artificial Intelligence / data management storage

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The right to liberty cannot undermine a survivor’s dignity, voice and difficult quest for justice

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought,” said John Rawls in A Theory of Justice. The American political philosopher’s line is easy to admire yet hard to practice. When an institution cannot be trusted to hear a wronged person, the old maxim justice delayed is justice denied begins to sound less like a warning than a description. For nearly a quarter of a century, Bilkis Bano, a survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots who was gang-raped by 11 men while pregnant and lost some members of her family, has had to prove over and over again what happened to her was real, that it was a crime, and that the law should answer it. Each time, she has done so with a defiant courage that has become a testament to the Republic’s conscience. She now may have to do it again. On October 28, 2026, a Supreme Court Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale suspended the life sentences of two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering some members of her family, granting them bail pending their appeals. Ms. Bano told the media that she learnt of the order just a few days ago through the press. The counsel for the two men later issued a statement on November 21, rejecting Ms. Bano’s allegation that she was kept in the dark about the proceedings but asserting that she was not party even in High Court. “It is still baffling to me that for the second time after this order was passed, I have not been summoned to appear before the Supreme Court, nor has anything been heard from me,” Ms. Bano said in a statement through her attorneys. It is a sentence that no citizen, for whatever reason he may have for taking the oath regardless of his opinion of the merits of the order, should find easy to read. Every word counts here. This case is designed to elicit both outrage and defensive responses. No one is found “not guilty” in the order. The principles, which were upheld by the Bombay High Court in 2017, remain the same. What the Bench has done is that it has merely suspended the sentences of the two men, Bipinchand Kanhaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, until their appeals are disposed of, by pointing out that both men have been in jail for over 17 years, one of them has a severe disability, and their appeals raise questions of fact and law that require examination. The Additional Solicitor General opposed the pleas. The convicts’ appeals against the High Court’s judgment are still to be decided. There is no objection to the order in the context of not subscribing to retributive or deterrent theories of punishment. However, at a time when there is talk of making the criminal justice system victim-centric, why was victimology forgotten in this case? That is the central question which survives despite the November 23, 2026 order by the same Bench releasing Siraj Pada, one of the convicts of the Sabarmati Express coach fire on similar grounds.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Gujarat / riots / crime, law and justice / sexual assault / court / media / judiciary (system of justice) / prison / criminal / constitution / human rights / Mumbai / government

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Employees of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), under the banner of a joint action committee of officers and workers’ organisations, launched an agitation in Kannur on Monday (November 23) demanding the withdrawal of the suspension of sub-engineer Satheesh Babu in connection with a brief power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph on Saturday (November 21).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Hundreds of employees and officers from various KSEB offices joined the protest, with the organisations warning that the agitation would continue until the suspension was revoked. They also indicated that the protest could be extended across the State if the management failed to reconsider its decision. The employees said the power supply had been disrupted for only about nine minutes as part of urgent maintenance work after a potentially dangerous fault was detected in an 11 kV feeder supplying the Kannur town area. They maintained that the interruption was necessary to avert a possible accident and that the required information had been communicated to consumers in advance through the outage management system and WhatsApp groups. They alleged that neither the division office nor the section office had been informed about the Minister’s programme and that there was no question of deliberately disrupting the power supply. They also said that Mr. Babu had submitted an explanation when the authorities sought his response, but he was suspended without a proper preliminary inquiry. The controversy erupted after the power disruption during the Electricity Minister’s programme at Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21. MLA T.O. Mohanan, who was present at the event, lodged a complaint with the KSEB chairman alleging deliberate disruption of the power supply. The suspension followed the complaint. Inaugurating the protest in front of the KSEB office in Kannur, MLA K.V. Sumesh described the suspension as arbitrary, undemocratic and an insult to the dignity of the employees. He demanded its immediate withdrawal and warned that failure to do so would lead to a strong public agitation across the State. He questioned the rationale behind suspecting an employee of deliberately disrupting power supply for political reasons, irrespective of which political front was in power.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Employees could not be expected to compromise safety procedures because a Minister or an elected representative was attending a programme,” he said.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Jana Sena Party Councillors, supporters opposed the party’s decision to elect Bojja Venkateswara Rao as Pithapuram Municipal Vice-Chairman on the grounds of being a newcomer to the party.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rift within the Jana Sena Party boiled over into open violence in Pithapuram on Monday as a bitter power struggle over the Municipal vice-chairman post culminated in the alleged assault of Veeramareddy Chakri, the personal assistant of JSP’s Kakinada MP Tangella Uday Srinivas, by party supporters. In a purported video, JSP supporters are seen grabbing Mr. Chakri by his collar and repeatedly attacking him outside the Pithapuram municipal office. The incident occurred when the MP was outside the municipal office, where JSP councillors raised slogans against his recommendation of Bojja Venkateswara Rao’s for the vice-chairman post. However, a war of words among the JSP councillors began inside the municipal office when one councillor proposed Mr Venkateswara Rao’s name for the vice-chairman post, and the MP supported it. Of the 18 councillors who recently won in the local body polls, only six backed the move. Others disagreed with the choice, saying Mr Venkateswara Rao is a “newcomer” because he joined the party from the YSRCP after the 2024 general elections. Later, JSP councillors proposed Pindi Sandhya’s name for the vice-chairman post. Senior party leader in the municipal council, Reddem Ramarao, rejected Mr. Venkateswara Rao’s candidature, claiming that the latter joined the party only after the 2024 general elections and that many senior leaders are eligible for the post. He backed Ms. Sandhya for the post. Senior leader Pendem Dorababu and Mr. Uday Srinivas attempted to convince the party councillors, after which councillors withdrew their proposal for Ms. Sandhya as vice-chairperson. “Venkateswara Rao has been elected as vice-chairman of Pithapuram Municipality unanimously,” Election Officer Sk. Mahaboob Sharif told The Hindu . After the elections, JSP supporters have staged a dharna in front of Pithapuram municipal office, raising slogans against Mr. Uday Srinivas for offering the vice-chairman post to a newcomer.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Besides, JSP won 18 seats out of a total of 36 wards in Pithapuram municipality in Kakinada district; TDP won six seats while their partner BJP won a single seat in the recently concluded municipal election. However, as many as ten independent candidates, believed to be rebels of the NDA alliance, became councillors.
